units.zh: 傅玄
units.en: Fu Xuan
units.literal: Fu Xuan.

units.zh: 傅玄，字休奕，北地泥陽人也。
units.en: Fu Xuan, whose courtesy name was Xiuyi, came from Niyang in Beidi commandery.
units.literal: Fu Xuan, style name Xiuyi, was a man of Niyang in Beidi.

units.zh: 祖燮，漢漢陽太守。
units.en: His grandfather, Fu Xie, had served the Han as prefect of Hanyang.
units.literal: His grandfather Xie was Han dynasty Prefect of Hanyang.

units.zh: 父幹，魏扶風太守。
units.en: His father, Fu Gan, was prefect of Fufeng under the Wei.
units.literal: His father Gan was Wei dynasty Prefect of Fufeng.

units.zh: 玄少孤貧，博學善屬文，解鐘律。
units.en: Orphaned and poor in his youth, Fu Xuan nevertheless read widely, wrote well, and had a firm grasp of bells and musical temperament.
units.literal: Xuan in youth was orphaned and poor, broadly learned and good at composing texts, and understood bells and musical pitch.

units.zh: 性剛勁亮直，不能容人之短。
units.en: He was by nature stern, outspoken, and upright, and he had little patience for other men's faults.
units.literal: By nature he was rigid, forceful, bright, and straight, and could not accommodate others' shortcomings.

units.zh: 郡上計吏再舉孝廉，太尉辟，皆不就。
units.en: The commandery's clerk on capital duty twice nominated him as filially pious and incorrupt, and the grand commandant summoned him to office, but he declined every time.
units.literal: The commandery's reporting clerk twice recommended him as Filially Pious and Incorrupt; the Grand Commandant summoned him; in each case he did not take office.

units.zh: 州舉秀才，除郎中，與東海繆施俱以時譽選入著作，撰集《魏書》。
units.en: The province then recommended him as an outstanding scholar, and he received appointment as a gentleman of the palace. Together with Mou Shi of Donghai he was chosen, on the strength of his reputation, for the historiography office, where he helped compile the History of Wei.
units.literal: The province nominated him as cultivated talent; he was appointed gentleman of the palace, and together with Mou Shi of Donghai, on contemporary reputation both were selected to enter the editorial office and compile the History of Wei.

units.zh: 後參安東、衛軍軍事，轉溫令，再遷弘農太守，領典農校尉。
units.en: He later served on the staffs of the generals who maintained the east and who guarded the army, became magistrate of Wen, was promoted twice and became governor of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of colonel director of agriculture.
units.literal: Later he joined staff on military affairs for the General Who Maintains the East and the General Who Guards the Army, was transferred to be magistrate of Wen, twice promoted to governor of Hongnong, and concurrent colonel director of agriculture.

units.zh: 所居稱職，數上書陳便宜，多所匡正。
units.en: In every post he earned a reputation for competence; he sent up memorial after memorial on practical reforms, and much of what he urged was put right.
units.literal: Wherever he dwelt in office he was called competent; repeatedly he submitted memorials stating conveniences, and many things were corrected through him.

units.zh: 五等建，封鶉觚男。
units.en: When the five-tier nobility was instituted, he was enfeoffed as baron of Chungu.
units.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as baron of Chungu.

units.zh: 武帝為晉王，以玄為散騎常侍。
units.en: While Emperor Wu was still king of Jin, he appointed Fu Xuan cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu was King of Jin, he appointed Xuan cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

units.zh: 及受禪，進爵為子，加附馬都尉。
units.en: After the abdication, Fu Xuan's noble rank was raised to viscount, and he was also given the title of chief commandant of attendant cavalry.
units.literal: When [he] received the abdication, [Xuan's] noble rank was advanced to viscount, and he was additionally given chief commandant of attendant cavalry.

units.zh: 帝初即位，廣納直言，開不諱之路，玄及散騎常侍皇甫陶共掌諫職。
units.en: At the beginning of the reign the emperor welcomed blunt counsel and declared that nothing was off limits for remonstrance; Fu Xuan and the cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Huangfu Tao were jointly charged with that advisory role.
units.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, he broadly accepted straight speech and opened a road on which nothing was taboo; Xuan together with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Huangfu Tao jointly held the remonstrance duty.

units.zh: 玄上疏曰：「臣聞先王之臨天下也，明其大教，長其義節。
units.en: Fu Xuan presented a memorial that began: "I have heard that when the kings of old faced the realm, they made plain the great moral teaching and nurtured a sense of duty and integrity.
units.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that when former kings faced all under Heaven, they clarified their great teaching and extended righteousness and integrity.

units.zh: 道化隆于上，清議行於下，上下相奉，人懷義心。
units.en: The transforming power of the Way flourished at court, while honest public opinion held sway in the countryside; high and low reinforced each other, and every man carried a sense of what was right.
units.literal: The way's transforming influence flourished above, pure discussion was practiced below, above and below mutually upheld one another, and people cherished a mind for righteousness.

units.zh: 亡秦蕩滅先王之制，以法術相禦，而義心亡矣。
units.en: The fallen Qin had torn down the institutions of the earlier kings, governed by legalist tricks and coercive technique, and in the process destroyed the moral conscience of the people.
units.literal: The perished Qin swept away former kings' institutions, used statutes and methods to control one another, and the mind for righteousness was lost.

units.zh: 近者魏武好法術，而天下貴刑名；
units.en: In our own day Emperor Wu of Wei doted on legalist methods, and the empire learned to prize harsh law and clever nomenclature over everything else.
units.literal: In recent times Emperor Wu of Wei favored statutes and methods, and all under Heaven esteemed punishments and names.

units.zh: 魏文慕通達，而天下賤守節。
units.en: Emperor Wen admired worldly sophistication, and the world came to despise men who clung stubbornly to principle.
units.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei admired all-round penetration, and all under Heaven slighted holding to integrity.

units.zh: 其後綱維不攝，而虛無放誕之論盈於朝野，使天下無復清議，而亡秦之病復發於今。
units.en: Discipline then collapsed, empty speculation and reckless talk flooded court and country, honest opinion fell silent, and the moral sickness that had destroyed Qin has broken out again in our time.
units.literal: Afterwards the net cords did not bind, and empty, wild, unrestrained discourse filled court and countryside, causing all under Heaven no longer to have pure discussion, and the malady of the perished Qin to break out again in the present.

units.zh: 陛下聖德，龍興受禪，弘堯、舜之化，開正直之路，體夏禹之至儉，綜殷周之典文，臣詠歎而已，將又奚言！
units.en: Your Majesty has risen with dragon virtue to accept the abdication; you have widened the influence of Yao and Shun, opened a path for the upright, embodied the frugality of Yu of Xia, and drawn together the classical learning of Yin and Zhou. I could do nothing but sing your praise—what more is left for me to say?
units.literal: Your Majesty, of sagely virtue—rising as a dragon and receiving the abdication—you spread Yao and Shun's transformation, open a road for the upright, embody Great Yu of Xia's utmost frugality, and compile the canonical texts of Yin and Zhou; your subject would only chant praise—what more is there to say!

units.zh: 惟未舉清遠有禮之臣，以敦風節；
units.en: Only this remains: you have not yet raised up ministers who combine purity, depth, and ritual decorum, men who could give backbone to public conduct;
units.literal: Only you have not yet promoted ministers who are pure, far-reaching, and observant of propriety, in order to thicken custom and integrity;

units.zh: 未退虛鄙，以懲不恪，臣是以猶敢有言。」
units.en: nor have you cleared away the hollow and the mean to punish slackness—and for that reason I still presume to speak."
units.literal: nor have you dismissed the empty and base to punish lack of reverence—therefore your subject for this reason still dares to have words."

units.zh: 詔報曰：「舉清遠有禮之臣者，此尤今之要也。」
units.en: The court answered with an edict: "Promoting men who are pure, serious, and observant of ritual is precisely what the age most urgently needs."
units.literal: The edict replied: "To promote ministers who are pure, far-reaching, and observant of propriety—this is especially what is essential today."

units.zh: 乃使玄草詔進之。
units.en: He thereupon told Fu Xuan to draft an edict carrying the policy forward.
units.literal: Then he had Xuan draft an edict to advance them.

units.zh: 玄復上疏曰：臣聞舜舉五臣，無為而化，用人得其要也。
units.en: Fu Xuan submitted another memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Shun elevated five ministers, the realm was transformed through effortless governance because he put the right men in the essential posts.
units.literal: Xuan again submitted a memorial saying: Your subject has heard that Shun raised up five ministers, and through non-action they transformed the people—this was because in employing men he grasped what mattered.

units.zh: 天下群司猥多，不可不審得其人也。
units.en: Offices throughout the realm are far too numerous; we cannot fail to choose the right men for each one.
units.literal: Under Heaven the host of offices is excessively numerous; one cannot but carefully obtain the right men for them.

units.zh: 不得其人，一日則損不貲，況積日乎！
units.en: When the wrong man holds a post, even a single day brings incalculable harm, to say nothing of months and years.
units.literal: If one does not obtain the right men, in a single day the loss is incalculable—how much more if days accumulate!

units.zh: 典謨曰「無曠庶官」，言職之不可久廢也。
units.en: The Canon of Yu says, "Let no office stand vacant," meaning that duties must not long go unfilled.
units.literal: The Canon of Yu says, "Let no common office stand vacant"—meaning that duties must not long be abandoned.

units.zh: 諸有疾病滿百日不差，宜令去職，優其禮秩而寵存之，既差而後更用。
units.en: Officials who remain ill for a full hundred days without improvement should leave their posts, but retain honorable rank and stipend until they recover and can serve again.
units.literal: All who have illness for a full hundred days without recovery ought to be ordered to leave office, favored in ritual rank and kept in honor, and only after recovery employed again.

units.zh: 臣不廢職于朝，國無曠官之累，此王政之急也。
units.en: If no one abandons his post at court, the state will not suffer from unfilled offices; this is among the most pressing tasks of royal government.
units.literal: If your subject does not abandon duties at court, the state will have no burden of vacant offices—this is the urgency of royal government.

units.zh: 臣聞先王分士農工商以經國制事，各一其業而殊其務。
units.en: Your subject has heard that the ancient kings divided society into scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants to govern the state, each group devoted to one calling and its distinct duties.
units.literal: Your subject has heard that former kings divided scholar, farmer, artisan, and merchant to order the state and regulate affairs, each fixing on one calling and distinguishing its tasks.

units.zh: 自士已上子弟，為之立太學以教之，選明師以訓之，各隨其才優劣而授用之。
units.en: For sons of the scholar class and above, they founded the Imperial Academy, chose able teachers, and appointed each according to his talent, whether high or low.
units.literal: From scholars upward, for their sons and younger brothers they established the Imperial Academy to teach them, selected bright teachers to instruct them, and according to each one's talent, superior or inferior, conferred and employed them.

units.zh: 農以豐其食，工以足其器，商賈以通其貨。
units.en: Farmers filled the granaries, artisans supplied tools, and merchants moved goods through trade.
units.literal: Farmers to enrich their food, artisans to complete their tools, and merchants to circulate their goods.

units.zh: 故雖天下之大，兆庶之眾，無有一人遊手。
units.en: Thus even in a vast realm with multitudes of people, no one was left idle.
units.literal: Therefore though the realm was vast and the myriad people numerous, not one person was idle-handed.

units.zh: 分數之法，周備如此。
units.en: The Zhou system of allotment was complete in just this fashion.
units.literal: The method of division and allotment was complete in Zhou in just this way.

units.zh: 漢、魏不定其分，百官子弟不修經藝而務交遊，未知蒞事而坐享天祿；
units.en: Han and Wei never fixed these divisions. Sons of officials neglected the classics for socializing, took office without knowing their duties, and still drew the state stipend;
units.literal: Han and Wei did not fix their divisions; sons and younger brothers of the hundred officials did not cultivate the classics and arts but devoted themselves to socializing, not yet knowing how to take office yet sitting and enjoying Heaven's stipends;

units.zh: 農工之業多廢，或逐淫利而離其事；
units.en: farming and craftsmanship were widely neglected, and many left their proper work to chase illicit profit;
units.literal: the occupations of farming and craftsmanship were largely abandoned, or men pursued illicit profit and left their proper tasks;

units.zh: 徒系名於太學，然不聞先王之風。
units.en: they were enrolled in name at the Imperial Academy yet never learned the ways of the ancient kings.
units.literal: they were merely tied by name to the Imperial Academy, yet did not hear the wind of the former kings.

units.zh: 今聖明之政資始，而漢、魏之失未改，散官眾而學校未設，遊手多而親農者少，工器不盡其宜。
units.en: Your enlightened rule has only just begun, yet the errors of Han and Wei remain uncorrected: supernumerary posts abound while schools go unfounded, idlers multiply while farmers dwindle, and tools are not put to proper use.
units.literal: Now the sage and bright government is just beginning, yet the faults of Han and Wei have not been corrected: supernumerary offices are many while schools are not established, idlers are many while those who personally farm are few, and tools and vessels do not fully suit their uses.

units.zh: 臣以為亟定其制，通計天下若干人為士，足以副在官之吏；
units.en: I urge that the system be fixed at once: calculate how many men the realm needs as scholars, enough to fill the assisting ranks of government;
units.literal: Your subject holds that one should urgently fix the system, calculate throughout the realm how many men should be scholars, enough to assist the officials in office;

units.zh: 若干人為農，三年足有一年之儲；
units.en: how many as farmers, so that three years' labor yields one year's full stores;
units.literal: how many men as farmers, so that in three years there is enough for one year's stores;

units.zh: 若干人為工，足其器用；
units.en: how many as artisans, enough to supply all needed tools;
units.literal: how many men as artisans, enough for their tools and implements;

units.zh: 若干人為商賈，足以通貨而已。
units.en: and how many as merchants, enough only to keep goods in circulation.
units.literal: how many men as merchants, enough merely to circulate goods.

units.zh: 尊儒尚學，貴農賤商，此皆事業之要務也。
units.en: Honoring Confucian learning, esteeming scholarship, valuing agriculture and keeping commerce low—these are essential priorities for every calling.
units.literal: Honoring Confucian learning, esteeming study, valuing farming and depreciating commerce—these are all essential tasks of the calling.

units.zh: 前皇甫陶上事，欲令賜拜散官皆課使親耕，天下享足食之利。
units.en: Earlier Huangfu Tao proposed that all men granted supernumerary appointments be required to farm in person, so the realm would enjoy the benefit of full granaries.
units.literal: Earlier Huangfu Tao submitted a proposal wishing to have all those granted and appointed to supernumerary posts compelled to farm in person, so that all under Heaven would enjoy the benefit of full food.

units.zh: 禹、稷躬稼，祚流後世，是以《明堂》、《月令》著帝藉之制。
units.en: Yu and Ji worked the fields themselves, and their blessing endured for ages; hence the Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances prescribe the emperor's sacred plowing.
units.literal: Yu and Ji personally plowed; their blessings flowed to later ages, and therefore the Bright Hall and Monthly Ordinances record the system of the emperor's sacred field.

units.zh: 伊尹古之名臣，耕於有莘；
units.en: Yi Yin, a famed minister of antiquity, plowed at Youxin;
units.literal: Yi Yin was an ancient famed minister who plowed at Youxin;

units.zh: 晏嬰齊之大夫，避莊公之難，亦耕于海濱。
units.en: Yan Ying, a minister of Qi, fled Duke Zhuang's troubles and likewise farmed on the seashore.
units.literal: Yan Ying was a grandee of Qi; fleeing Duke Zhuang's troubles, he also plowed on the seashore.

units.zh: 昔者聖帝明王，賢佐俊士，皆嘗從事于農矣。
units.en: Sage emperors, enlightened kings, worthy ministers, and outstanding scholars all once worked the fields.
units.literal: In former times sage emperors and enlightened kings, worthy assistants and outstanding scholars, all once engaged in farming.

units.zh: 王人賜官，冗散無事者，不督使學，則當使耕，無緣放之使坐食百姓也。
units.en: For royal kin granted office who hold idle supernumerary posts, if they are not required to study, they should be required to farm; there is no excuse for letting them live off the people without work.
units.literal: For royal men granted office, those supernumerary and idle, if not supervised and made to study, then they ought to be made to farm—there is no reason to release them to sit and eat off the common people.

units.zh: 今文武之官既眾，而拜賜不在職者又多，加以服役為兵，不得耕稼，當農者之半，南面食祿者參倍於前。
units.en: Civil and military posts are already numerous, supernumerary appointees abound, and many who should farm are kept from the fields by military service, so that half the men who ought to till the soil are lost while capital stipendiaries have tripled.
units.literal: Now civil and military officials are already numerous, and those granted appointment who are not in active posts are also many; add to this service as soldiers, unable to plow and sow—those who should be farmers are cut in half, while stipendiaries at the capital are three times what they were before.

units.zh: 使冗散之官農，而收其租稅，家得其實，而天下之穀可以無乏矣。
units.en: If idle officials were put to farming and their harvest taxed, households would prosper and the realm's grain supply would never fail.
units.literal: If supernumerary officials were made to farm and their rent and tax collected, each household would obtain its substance, and the grain of all under Heaven could be without shortage.

units.zh: 夫家足食，為子則孝，為父則慈，為兄則友，為弟則悌。
units.en: When households have enough to eat, sons are filial, fathers are kindly, elder brothers are friendly, and younger brothers are deferential.
units.literal: When households have full food, as sons they are filial, as fathers they are kindly, as elder brothers they are friendly, as younger brothers they are deferential.

units.zh: 天下足食，則仁義之教可不令而行也。
units.en: When the realm has full granaries, the teaching of humaneness and righteousness will spread without need of command.
units.literal: When all under Heaven has full food, then the teaching of humaneness and righteousness can proceed without being commanded.

units.zh: 為政之要，計人而置官，分人而授事，士農工商之分不可斯須廢也。
units.en: The essence of government is to count the people, assign offices, divide labor, and assign tasks; the division of scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants must never be set aside even for a moment.
units.literal: The essential of governing is to count men and then set offices, divide men and then assign tasks—the division of scholar, farmer, artisan, and merchant must not for an instant be abandoned.

units.zh: 若未能精其防制，計天下文武之官足為副貳者使學，其餘皆歸之于農。
units.en: If the controls cannot yet be perfected, count those civil and military officials fit to serve as deputies and require them to study; all others should be returned to the fields.
units.literal: If one cannot yet refine the safeguards and controls, calculate the civil and military officials throughout the realm who are sufficient to serve as deputies and have them study; all the rest should be returned to farming.

units.zh: 若百工商賈有長者，亦皆歸之于農。
units.en: Elders among artisans and merchants should likewise be returned to farming.
units.literal: If among artisans and merchants there are elders, they too should all be returned to farming.

units.zh: 務農若此，何有不贍乎！
units.en: If agriculture is pursued in this way, how could the realm fail to prosper!
units.literal: If farming is pursued in this way, how could there be anything but plenty!

units.zh: 《虞書》曰：「三載考績，三考黜陟幽明。」
units.en: The Book of Yu says: "Examine achievements every three years; after three examinations promote the worthy and remove the unfit."
units.literal: The Book of Yu says: "Every three years examine achievements; after three examinations promote the bright and demote the dim."

units.zh: 是為九年之後乃有遷敘也。
units.en: This means that promotion in rank comes only after nine years.
units.literal: This means that only after nine years is there advancement in rank.

units.zh: 故居官久，則念立慎終之化，居不見久，則競為一切之政。
units.en: When men hold office long, they learn to finish what they begin with care; when terms are too short, they scramble for quick expedients.
units.literal: Therefore if one dwells long in office, one thinks to establish the transformation of careful completion; if one does not dwell long enough to be seen, one competes in making expedient policies.

units.zh: 六年之限，日月淺近，不周黜陟。
units.en: A six-year term is too brief to carry out a full round of promotions and demotions.
units.literal: A limit of six years—the days and months are shallow and near, and do not complete promotion and demotion.

units.zh: 陶之所上，義合古制。
units.en: Huangfu Tao's proposal accords with the ancient system in principle.
units.literal: What Tao submitted accords in principle with the ancient system.

units.zh: 夫儒學者，王教之首也。
units.en: Confucian learning stands at the head of royal instruction.
units.literal: Confucian learning is the head of royal teaching.

units.zh: 尊其道，貴其業，重其選，猶恐化之不崇；
units.en: Even when its Way is honored, its calling esteemed, and its selection weighted with care, one still fears the moral transformation will not rise high enough;
units.literal: Honoring its Way, esteeming its calling, and weighting its selection—one still fears that the transformation will not be lofty enough;

units.zh: 忽而不以為急，臣懼日有陵遲而不覺也。
units.en: if it is neglected and not treated as urgent, I fear the teaching will decline day by day without anyone noticing.
units.literal: if it is neglected and not treated as urgent, your subject fears that day by day there will be decline without awareness.

units.zh: 仲尼有言：「人能弘道，非道弘人。」
units.en: Confucius said: "It is men who enlarge the Way, not the Way that enlarges men."
units.literal: Confucius had a saying: "It is the man who enlarges the Way, not the Way that enlarges the man."

units.zh: 然則尊其道者，非惟尊其書而已，尊其人之謂也。
units.en: To honor the Way, then, is not merely to honor its books but to honor the men who embody it.
units.literal: Accordingly, to honor its Way is not merely to honor its books—it means to honor its men.

units.zh: 貴其業者，不妄教非其人也。
units.en: To esteem the calling is not to teach those who are unfit for it.
units.literal: To esteem its calling is not to teach rashly those who are not its men.

units.zh: 重其選者，不妄用非其人也。
units.en: To weight selection is not to appoint those who are unfit.
units.literal: To weight its selection is not to employ rashly those who are not its men.

units.zh: 若此，而學校之綱舉矣。
units.en: If this is done, the guiding principle of the schools will be established.
units.literal: If it is like this, then the guiding principle of the schools is raised.

units.zh: 書奏，帝下詔曰：「二常侍懇懇於所論，可謂乃心欲佐益時事者也。
units.en: When the memorial reached him, the emperor issued an edict: "The two attendant cavaliers have argued their case with real conviction; they clearly mean to put their hearts into improving the business of government.
units.literal: When the document was presented, the emperor issued an edict saying: "The two regular attendants have been earnest in what they discussed; they may be called to give their hearts wishing to aid and benefit the affairs of the times.

units.zh: 而主者率以常制裁之，豈得不使發憤耶！
units.en: Yet the bureaus keep folding everything back into routine paperwork—no wonder honest men boil with frustration!
units.literal: Yet those in charge routinely dispose of it by regular procedures—how could that not make one resent it in anger!

units.zh: 二常侍所論，或舉其大較而未備其條目，亦可便令作之，然後主者八坐廣共研精。
units.en: What the two cavaliers propose may state the broad outline without filling in every clause; let them draft a fuller version, then have the responsible ministers and the eight senior seats work through the details together.
units.literal: What the two regular attendants debated perhaps raises its general drift but does not complete each item; you may also conveniently have them compose it, after which the presiding officials and the eight seats should together broadly refine it.

units.zh: 凡關言於人主，人臣之所至難。
units.en: Speaking truth to the sovereign is the hardest thing a subject can do.
units.literal: Generally, matters that concern speaking to the human ruler are what subjects find hardest.

units.zh: 而人主若不能虛心聽納，自古忠臣直士之所慷慨，至使杜口結舌。
units.en: If the ruler will not listen with an open mind, loyal ministers have always grown desperate and ended by holding their tongues altogether.
units.literal: If the human ruler cannot listen and accept with an empty mind, from antiquity loyal ministers and straight men have for this reason been stirred to passion, to the point of sealing their mouths and binding their tongues.

units.zh: 每念於此，未嘗不歎息也。
units.en: Whenever I think of it, I cannot help but sigh.
units.literal: Whenever I think of this, I have never failed to sigh.

units.zh: 故前詔敢有直言，勿有所距，庶幾得以發懞補過，獲保高位。
units.en: That is why my earlier edict invited blunt speech and forbade anyone to block it—I hoped ignorance might be aired, faults corrected, and high office kept secure.
units.literal: Therefore the earlier edict allowed daring straight speech and forbade blocking it, hoping thereby to air ignorance and mend faults, and obtain preservation of high rank.

units.zh: 苟言有偏善，情在忠益，雖文辭有謬誤，言語有失得，皆當曠然恕之。
units.en: Whenever a remark contains even a partial good point and the speaker means loyalty and the public good, I should overlook clumsy wording or slips of the tongue and forgive him outright.
units.literal: If in what is said there is partial good, and the intent is in loyalty and benefit—even if diction has errors and speech has misses and gains—all should be broadly and clearly forgiven.

units.zh: 古人猶不拒誹謗，況皆善意在可採錄乎！
units.en: The ancients did not even refuse bitter criticism; how much less should I reject advice offered in good faith and worth taking down!
units.literal: The ancients still did not refuse slander; how much more when all are good intentions and there is something that can be selected and recorded!

units.zh: 近者孔晁、綦毋龢皆案以輕慢之罪，所以皆原，欲使四海知區區之朝無諱言之忌也。」
units.en: Not long ago Kong Chao and Qi Wu He were charged with disrespect; I pardoned them both so that the empire would see this court has no fear of plain speaking."
units.literal: Recently Kong Chao and Qi Wu He were both sentenced on the crime of slight disrespect; the reason they were all pardoned was to desire to let the four seas know that this humble court has no taboo against speaking one's mind."

units.zh: 俄遷侍中。
units.en: Soon afterward Fu Xuan was promoted to palace attendant.
units.literal: Soon after he was promoted to palace attendant.

units.zh: 初，玄進皇甫陶，及入而抵，玄以事與陶爭，言喧嘩，為有司所奏，二人竟坐免官，
units.en: Earlier, Fu Xuan had recommended Huangfu Tao, but once Tao took office the two men fell out; they quarreled loudly over policy until the authorities impeached them, and both were stripped of their posts.
units.literal: At first Xuan had recommended Huangfu Tao, but when [Tao] entered they clashed; Xuan over affairs quarrelled with Tao, words were noisy and clamorous, they were reported by the authorities, and in the end both sat and were dismissed from office.

units.zh: 泰始四年，以為御史中丞。
units.en: In the fourth year of Taishi, he was appointed metropolitan censor.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, he was appointed metropolitan censor.

units.zh: 時頗有水旱之災，玄復上疏曰：臣聞聖帝明王受命，天時未必無災，是以堯有九年之水，湯有七年之旱，惟能濟之以人事耳。
units.en: Floods and droughts were then plaguing the realm, and Fu Xuan submitted another memorial: "Your subject has heard that even sage emperors and enlightened kings who receive the Mandate may face calamity in the seasons of Heaven. Yao endured nine years of flood and Tang seven years of drought; only human effort could remedy such disasters."
units.literal: At that time there were rather frequent flood and drought disasters; Xuan again submitted a memorial saying: Your subject has heard that when sage emperors and enlightened kings receive the Mandate, the seasons of Heaven are not necessarily without disaster; therefore Yao had nine years of flood and Tang seven years of drought—only by remedying it through human effort.

units.zh: 故洪水滔天而免沈溺，野無生草而不困匱。
units.en: Thus though the floodwaters rose to Heaven, men were not drowned; though the wilds bore no living grass, the people were not left in want.
units.literal: Therefore though floodwaters rose to Heaven, men were spared drowning; though the wilds had no living grass, they were not distressed by want.

units.zh: 伏惟陛下聖德欽明，時小水旱，人未大饑，下祗畏之詔，求極意之言，同禹、湯之罪己，侔周文之夕惕。
units.en: Your Majesty's sage virtue shines with reverent clarity. Though the present floods and droughts are still modest and the people are not yet in great famine, you have issued an edict of awe seeking the utmost candid counsel, matching Yu and Tang in self-reproach and King Wen of Zhou in nightly vigilance.
units.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty's sage virtue is reverently bright; though the times have slight flood and drought and the people are not yet greatly famished, you have issued an edict of reverent awe seeking words of utmost intent, equal to Yu and Tang blaming themselves and matching King Wen of Zhou's evening vigilance.

units.zh: 臣伏歡喜，上便宜五事：其一曰，耕夫務多種而耕不熟，徒喪功力而無收。
units.en: I bow in joy and submit five practical proposals. The first: farmers strive to sow heavily yet the crops do not ripen, wasting labor without harvest.
units.literal: Your subject bows in joy and submits five practical proposals: the first says that farmers strive to sow much yet plow without ripening, vainly losing labor without harvest.

units.zh: 又舊兵持官牛者，官得六分，士得四分；
units.en: Formerly, for garrison farmer-soldiers using official oxen, the state received six parts and the soldier four;
units.literal: Further, formerly for soldier-farmers using official oxen, the office received six parts and the soldier four;

units.zh: 自持私牛者，與官中分，施行來久，眾心安之。
units.en: those using private oxen divided the harvest equally with the state. This had long been in force and the men were content.
units.literal: those using their own private oxen divided equally with the office; this had long been in force and the multitude was settled in mind.

units.zh: 今一朝減持官牛者，官得八分，士得二分；
units.en: Now, overnight, for those using official oxen the state takes eight parts and the soldier two;
units.literal: Now in one morning those using official oxen were reduced: the office receives eight parts and the soldier two;

units.zh: 持私牛及無牛者，官得七分，士得三分，人失其所，必不歡樂。
units.en: for those using private oxen or no oxen at all, the state takes seven parts and the soldier three. The men lose what is rightfully theirs and cannot be content.
units.literal: for those using private oxen and those without oxen, the office receives seven parts and the soldier three; men lose what is theirs and will surely not be glad.

units.zh: 臣愚以為宜佃兵持官牛者與四分，持私牛與官中分，則天下兵作歡然悅樂，愛惜成穀，無有損棄之憂。
units.en: I hold that garrison farmer-soldiers using official oxen should receive four parts, and those using private oxen should divide equally with the state. Then soldier-farmers throughout the realm would work gladly, cherish the grain they produced, and there would be no fear of waste.
units.literal: Your subject foolishly holds that garrison farmer-soldiers using official oxen should receive four parts, and those using private oxen should divide equally with the office; then soldier-farmers throughout the realm would gladly rejoice, cherish the grain they produced, and there would be no worry of waste and loss.

units.zh: 其二曰，以二千石雖奉務農之詔，猶不勤心以盡地利。
units.en: The second: though prefect-level officials receive edicts to promote farming, they still do not earnestly exploit the land's full potential.
units.literal: The second says that though the two-thousand-bushel officials receive the edict to promote farming, they still do not earnestly apply their hearts to exhaust the land's advantage.

units.zh: 昔漢氏以墾田不實，征殺二千石以十數。
units.en: Formerly the Han executed more than ten prefects by imperial order for falsely reporting reclaimed fields.
units.literal: Formerly the Han, because reclaimed fields were not reported truthfully, executed by imperial order more than ten two-thousand-bushel officials.

units.zh: 臣愚以為宜申漢氏舊典，以警戒天下郡縣，皆以死刑督之。
units.en: I hold that the Han precedent should be renewed to warn every commandery and county in the realm, with the death penalty enforcing compliance.
units.literal: Your subject foolishly holds that one ought to renew the Han old precedent to warn all commanderies and counties under Heaven, all supervised by the death penalty.

units.zh: 其三曰，以魏初未留意于水事，先帝統百揆，分河堤為四部，並本凡五謁者，以水功至大，與農事並興，非一人所周故也。
units.en: The third: in early Wei water affairs were neglected. The late emperor, directing all ministries, divided river dikes into four departments, making five ushers in all, because water works are vast and must advance together with farming—more than one man can oversee.
units.literal: The third says that at the beginning of Wei they did not attend to water affairs; the late emperor directed all the ministries, divided the river dikes into four departments, and with the original office there were in all five ushers, because water works are extremely great and rise together with farming—this is not what one man can comprehensively oversee.

units.zh: 今謁者一人之力，行天下諸水，無時得遍。
units.en: Now one usher's strength, traveling to every waterway in the realm, cannot possibly reach them all in time.
units.literal: Now the strength of one usher, traveling to all waters under Heaven, has no time to reach everywhere.

units.zh: 伏見河堤謁者車誼不知水勢，轉為他職，更選知水者代之。
units.en: I observe that the river-dike usher Che Yi does not understand water conditions. He should be transferred to another post and a man who knows water selected in his place.
units.literal: I bow and observe that the river-dike usher Che Yi does not know water conditions; he should be transferred to another post and another who knows water selected to replace him.

units.zh: 可分為五部，使各精其方宜。
units.en: The work should be divided into five departments, each mastering the conditions of its region.
units.literal: They can be divided into five departments, so that each may master the local conditions of his region.

units.zh: 其四曰，古以步百為畝，今以二百四十步為一畝，所覺過倍。
units.en: The fourth: antiquity reckoned one mu at one hundred paces; now one mu is two hundred forty paces, so reported acreage more than doubles.
units.literal: The fourth says that antiquity took one hundred paces as a mu; now two hundred forty paces make one mu—the acreage reported exceeds by more than double.

units.zh: 近魏初課田，不務多其頃畝，但務修其功力，故白田收至十餘斛，水田收數十斛。
units.en: In early Wei field assessment did not aim to inflate acreage but to improve labor; dry fields then yielded more than ten hu and paddy fields several tens of hu.
units.literal: Near the beginning of Wei in assessing fields, they did not strive to increase the qing and mu but only strove to repair labor power; therefore dry fields yielded more than ten hu and paddy fields several tens of hu.

units.zh: 自頃以來，日增田頃畝之課，而田兵益甚，功不能修理，至畝數斛已還，或不足以償種。
units.en: Recently the assessed acreage has been increased daily while soldier-farmers multiply, yet labor cannot be properly applied; yields fall to only a few hu per mu, sometimes not even enough to repay the seed.
units.literal: From recent times onward, daily increasing the assessment of field qing and mu, while soldier-farmers grew ever more numerous, labor could not be maintained and repaired; per mu there were only several hu in return, or not enough even to repay seed.

units.zh: 非與曩時異天地，橫遇災害也，其病正在於務多頃畝而功不修耳。
units.en: Heaven and Earth have not changed since former times, nor has disaster struck by chance; the trouble lies precisely in chasing inflated acreage while neglecting labor.
units.literal: It is not that Heaven and Earth differ from former times or that disaster was met by chance; the disease lies precisely in striving for more qing and mu while labor is not maintained.

units.zh: 竊見河堤謁者石恢甚精練水事及田事，知其利害，乞中書召恢，委曲問其得失，必有所補益。
units.en: I observe that the river-dike usher Shi Hui is highly skilled in water works and field management and understands their advantages and drawbacks. I beg the Secretariat to summon Shi Hui and question him in detail; he will surely offer useful counsel.
units.literal: I privately observe that the river-dike usher Shi Hui is very skilled in water affairs and field affairs and knows their gains and losses; I beg the Secretariat to summon Hui and question him in detail on gains and losses—there will surely be some benefit.

units.zh: 其五曰，臣以為胡夷獸心，不與華同，鮮卑最甚。
units.en: The fifth: I hold that the Hu and other barbarians have the hearts of beasts and are not like the Hua; the Xianbei are the worst of them.
units.literal: The fifth says that your subject holds the Hu and barbarians have beast hearts, not the same as the Hua; the Xianbei are most extreme.

units.zh: 本鄧艾苟欲取一時之利，不慮後患，使鮮卑數萬散居人間，此必為害之勢也。
units.en: Deng Ai, seeking only immediate profit without regard for later trouble, scattered tens of thousands of Xianbei among the people—a situation bound to become dangerous.
units.literal: Originally Deng Ai, wishing only to seize profit for one moment, did not consider later trouble, and had several tens of thousands of Xianbei scattered to dwell among the people—this is a situation that must become harmful.

units.zh: 秦州刺史胡烈素有恩信於西方，今烈往，諸胡雖已無惡，必且消弭，然獸心難保，不必其可久安也。
units.en: Hu Lie, prefect of Qin province, has long enjoyed favor and trust in the west. With Lie now posted there, the various Hu, though presently peaceful, will surely be pacified for the moment; yet beast hearts cannot be trusted, and long security is not assured.
units.literal: The prefect of Qin province, Hu Lie, has long had favor and trust in the west; now that Lie goes there, though the various Hu are already without malice, they will surely be pacified for the moment, yet beast hearts are hard to guarantee—not necessarily that they can long be secure.

units.zh: 若後有動釁，烈計能制之。
units.en: If trouble stirs later, Lie should be able to control it.
units.literal: If afterward there is stirring and provocation, Lie by plan can control it.

units.zh: 惟恐胡虜適困於討擊，便能東入安定，西赴武威，外名為降，可動復動。
units.en: I fear only that when the Hu are hard pressed by punitive attack, they can slip east into Anding or west into Wuwei; though nominally submitting, they can rise again whenever opportunity stirs them.
units.literal: I only fear that when the Hu enemy happens to be hard pressed by punitive attack, they can at once enter Anding to the east and go to Wuwei in the west; outwardly named as submitting, they can stir again whenever stirred.

units.zh: 此二郡非烈所制，則惡胡東西有窟穴浮游之地，故復為患，無以禁之也。
units.en: If these two commanderies are not under Lie's control, the hostile Hu will have lairs east and west in which to roam freely, become dangerous again, and cannot be restrained.
units.literal: If these two commanderies are not under Lie's control, then the wicked Hu east and west will have lairs and drifting places to roam; therefore they will again become a calamity, and there will be no means to restrain them.

units.zh: 宜更置一郡于高平川，因安定西州都尉募樂徙民，重其復除以充之，以通北道，漸以實邊。
units.en: A new commandery should be established in the Gaoping valley. Through the Anding West Province commandant, willing migrants should be recruited, granted heavy tax exemptions to settle there, the northern route opened, and the frontier gradually strengthened.
units.literal: One ought to establish another commandery at Gaoping River valley, relying on the Anding West Province commandant to recruit willing migrant people, weighting their tax exemptions to fill it, so as to open the northern route and gradually make solid the frontier.

units.zh: 詳議此二郡及新置郡，皆使並屬秦州，令烈得專禦邊之宜。
units.en: These two commanderies and the new commandery should be deliberated in detail and all placed under Qin province, so that Lie may have exclusive authority to manage frontier defense as circumstances require.
units.literal: Deliberate in detail on these two commanderies and the newly established commandery, all making them jointly subordinate to Qin province, so that Lie may exclusively apply what is fitting for defending the frontier.

units.zh: 詔曰：「得所陳便宜，言農事得失及水官興廢，又安邊禦胡政事寬猛之宜，申省周備，一二具之，此誠為國大本，當今急務也。
units.en: The emperor replied by edict: "Your practical proposals on the successes and failures of agriculture, on which water offices to keep or abolish, and on how to balance severity and leniency in securing the frontier against the Hu are set out with admirable clarity. These are indeed fundamental matters for the state and pressing tasks for today.
units.literal: An edict said: "Having received the conveniences you set forth—speaking of farming affairs' gains and losses and water offices' rise and fall, also the fit of lenience and severity in governing the frontiers and repelling the Hu—laid out clearly and completely item by item—this is truly the great root of the state and the urgent task of the present.

units.zh: 如所論皆善，深知乃心，廣思諸宜，動靜以聞也。」
units.en: If everything you argue is sound, know that I understand your intent; think through every suitable measure and keep me informed as circumstances change."
units.literal: If as you discuss all is good, I know deeply what is in your heart; think broadly on every suitable measure, and by movement and stillness report it."

units.zh: 五年，遷太僕。
units.en: In the fifth year of the reign he was promoted to grand coachman.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to grand coachman.

units.zh: 時比年不登，羌胡擾邊，詔公卿會議。
units.en: Harvests had failed year after year, Qiang and Hu raiders harried the frontier, and the court ordered the high ministers to convene for deliberation.
units.literal: At that time year after year the harvests did not ripen, the Qiang and Hu disturbed the borders, and an edict ordered dukes and ministers to meet in council.

units.zh: 玄應對所問，陳事切直，雖不盡施行，而常見優容。
units.en: Fu Xuan answered every question put to him with blunt, searching analysis; not all of his advice was adopted, but the throne regularly treated him with patience and favor.
units.literal: In answering what was asked Xuan stated matters incisively and directly; though not everything was fully put into practice, he was often shown favor and tolerance.

units.zh: 轉司隸校尉。
units.en: He was then transferred to the post of colonel director of retainers.
units.literal: He was transferred to colonel director of retainers.

units.zh: 獻皇后崩于弘訓宮，設喪位。
units.en: Empress Xian died in Hongxun Palace, and mourning stations were arranged for the rites.
units.literal: Empress Xian died in the Hongxun Palace, and mourning stations were set up.

units.zh: 舊制，司隸於端門外坐，在諸卿上，絕席。
units.en: By established precedent the colonel director of retainers took his seat outside the Duan Gate above the other ministers, on a separate mat that marked his precedence.
units.literal: By old regulation the colonel director of retainers sat outside the Duan Gate, above the various ministers, on a separate mat.

units.zh: 其入殿，按本品秩在諸卿下，以次坐，不絕席。
units.en: When he entered the main hall, his nominal rank placed him below the ministers in order of seating, without the privilege of a separate mat.
units.literal: When entering the hall, according to his original grade and rank he was below the various ministers, sitting in order, not on a separate mat.

units.zh: 而謁者以弘訓宮為殿內，制玄位在卿下。
units.en: The ushers treated Hongxun Palace as part of the inner palace and therefore assigned Fu Xuan a place below the ministers.
units.literal: But the usher took the Hongxun Palace as being inside the hall and regulated Xuan's seat to be below the ministers.

units.zh: 玄恚怒，厲聲色而責謁者。
units.en: Fu Xuan flared with rage and berated the ushers in a harsh voice.
units.literal: Xuan was angry and furious, and in severe voice and countenance rebuked the usher.

units.zh: 謁者妄稱尚書所處，玄對百僚而罵尚書以下。
units.en: The ushers falsely claimed the secretariat had fixed the seating; Fu Xuan then reviled the secretariat and everyone below it in full view of the court.
units.literal: The usher falsely claimed it was where the secretariat had placed him; Xuan in front of the hundred officials berated the secretariat downward.

units.zh: 御史中丞庾純奏玄不敬，玄又自表不以實，坐免官。
units.en: Metropolitan censor Yu Chun impeached him for disrespect; Fu Xuan's own written defense was deemed untruthful, and he was dismissed from office.
units.literal: Metropolitan censor Yu Chun memorialized that Xuan had been disrespectful; Xuan also self-reported not according to truth; by verdict he was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 然玄天性峻急，不能有所容；
units.en: By nature Fu Xuan was harsh and impatient, and he made allowance for no one.
units.literal: Yet Xuan by nature was steep and hasty and could accommodate nothing.

units.zh: 每有奏劾，或值日暮，捧白簡，整簪帶，竦踴不寐，坐而待旦。
units.en: Whenever he prepared an impeachment, even if night was falling, he would take up his white indictment tablet, straighten cap and sash, sit bolt upright without sleep, and wait for dawn.
units.literal: Whenever he had a memorial of impeachment, sometimes it happened to be dusk; he would grasp the white tablet, straighten hairpin and belt, stand bolt upright and leap, not sleep, and sit waiting for dawn.

units.zh: 於是貴遊懾伏，臺閣生風。
units.en: The great families trembled into submission, and a new austerity swept through the bureaus.
units.literal: Thereupon the noble and wandering were awed into submission, and the terraces and pavilions produced wind.

units.zh: 尋卒于家，時年六十二，諡曰剛。
units.en: He died at home not long afterward, aged sixty-two, with the posthumous name Gang, "the unyielding."
units.literal: Soon he died at home; at the time his age was sixty-two; his posthumous title was called Gang.

units.zh: 玄少時避難於河內，專心誦學，後雖顯貴，而著述不廢。
units.en: In his youth he had fled trouble to Henei and given himself entirely to study; even after he rose to high rank he never set scholarship aside.
units.literal: In youth Xuan took refuge from troubles in Henei and devoted his mind to reciting and learning; later although he was eminent and noble, yet writing was not abandoned.

units.zh: 撰論經國九流及三史故事，評斷得失，各為區例，名為《傅子》，為內、外、中篇，凡有四部、六錄，合百四十首，數十萬言，並文集百餘卷行於世。
units.en: He wrote treatises on statecraft and the nine schools of thought, drew lessons from the three histories, weighed right and wrong, and arranged his conclusions by topic in a work called the Fu zi, divided into inner, outer, and middle books—four sections, six registers, one hundred forty chapters and several hundred thousand characters—together with a literary collection of more than a hundred fascicles that circulated widely.
units.literal: He composed discourses on ordering the state and the nine currents and on stories from the three histories, judging gains and losses, each establishing categories and examples, named the Collected Master Fu—inner, outer, and middle sections—in all four parts, six registers, totaling 140 pieces, several hundred thousand graphs, together with a literary collection of over a hundred fascicles that circulated in the world.

units.zh: 玄初作內篇成，子咸以示司空王沈。
units.en: When Fu Xuan had finished the first part of the inner books, his son Fu Xian showed the manuscript to Wang Chen, the minister of works.
units.literal: When Xuan first finished composing the inner chapters, his son Xian showed them to Minister of Works Wang Chen.

units.zh: 沈與玄書曰：「省足下所著書，言富理濟，經綸政體，存重儒教，足以塞楊、墨之流遁，齊孫、孟于往代。
units.en: Wang Chen wrote to Fu Xuan: "I have read what you have written; the language is ample and the argument sound. In ordering the body politic you give due weight to Confucian teaching—enough to shut the door on the evasions of Yang Zhu and Mozi and to set Sunzi and Mencius on a par with the best of antiquity.
units.literal: Chen wrote to Xuan saying: "I have examined what you have written; the words are rich and the principles sustain; in ordering the threads of government it preserves and values Confucian teaching—enough to block the Yang and Mo schools' flow and evasion, and align Sun and Mencius with past ages.

units.zh: 每開卷，未嘗不歎息也。
units.en: Whenever I open the manuscript I find myself sighing in admiration.
units.literal: Whenever I open a scroll, I have never failed to sigh.

units.zh: 『不見賈生，自以過之，乃今不及』，信矣！」
units.en: As the saying goes, 'Before I met Jia Yi I thought I surpassed him; now I see I do not measure up'—how true that is!"
units.literal: Not having seen Master Jia, I thought I surpassed him; now I am not his equal'—how true!"

units.zh: 其後追封清泉侯。
units.en: He was later given the posthumous title of marquis of Qingquan.
units.literal: Afterwards he was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis of Qingquan.

units.zh: 子咸嗣。
units.en: His son Fu Xian inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Xian inherited.

units.zh: 子咸
units.en: Fu Xian
units.literal: Son Xian.

units.zh: =咸字長虞，剛簡有大節。
units.en: Fu Xian, courtesy name Changyu, was austere and plain-spoken and showed unbending integrity in great matters.
units.literal: Xian, style name Changyu, was stern and simple and had great integrity.

units.zh: 風格峻整，識性明悟，疾惡如仇，推賢樂善，常慕季文子、仲山甫之志。
units.en: His bearing was severe and composed, his judgment lucid; he hated wickedness as he would a personal enemy, lifted up the worthy, and delighted in the good, and he modeled himself on the aspirations of Ji Wenzi and Zhong Shanfu of old.
units.literal: His manner and pattern were stern and ordered, his knowledge and nature bright and perceptive; he hated evil as if an enemy, promoted the worthy and delighted in the good, and often admired the aims of Ji Wenzi and Zhong Shanfu.

units.zh: 好屬文論，雖綺麗不足，而言成規鑒。
units.en: He loved to write essays and memorials; they lacked ornamental brilliance, but every piece offered clear standards and sober judgment.
units.literal: He was fond of composing texts and disquisitions; though ornate beauty was insufficient, yet his words formed regulation and mirror.

units.zh: 潁川庾純常歎曰：「長虞之文近乎詩人之作矣！」
units.en: Yu Chun of Yingchuan used to exclaim, "Changyu's prose is almost what we call poetry!"
units.literal: Yu Chun of Yingchuan often sighed saying: "Changyu's texts are close to the work of the poets!"

units.zh: 咸甯初，襲父爵，拜太子洗馬，累遷尚書右丞。
units.en: Early in the Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed tutor to the heir apparent, and rose through several posts to right assistant in the secretariat.
units.literal: In the early Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed xianma (attendant) of the heir apparent, and by stages was promoted to right assistant of the secretariat.

units.zh: 出為冀州刺史，繼母杜氏不肯隨咸之官，自表解職。
units.en: When he was sent out as inspector of Ji, his stepmother, Lady Du, refused to accompany him to his post, so he asked to resign.
units.literal: He went out to be inspector of Ji Province; his stepmother Lady Du was unwilling to follow Xian to his post, so he personally memorialized requesting release from duty.

units.zh: 三旬之間，遷司徒左長史。
units.en: Within thirty days he was promoted to senior clerk on the left of the minister of education.
units.literal: Within thirty days he was promoted to senior clerk in the left of the minister of education.

units.zh: 時帝留心政事，詔訪朝臣政之損益。
units.en: The emperor was then intent on government and issued an edict asking the ministers what in current policy helped or harmed the realm.
units.literal: At that time the emperor applied his mind to government affairs; an edict inquired of court ministers about harm and benefit in administration.

units.zh: 咸上言曰：「陛下處至尊之位，而修布衣之事，親覽萬機，勞心日昃。
units.en: Fu Xian submitted a memorial: "Although Your Majesty occupies the highest throne, you still take on a commoner's workload, personally attending to every matter of government, laboring in mind until the sun stands in the west.
units.literal: Xian submitted words saying: "Your Majesty occupies the supremely honored position, yet cultivates common-cloth affairs, personally inspects ten thousand threads, and toils in mind until the sun slants.

units.zh: 在昔帝王，躬自菲薄，以利天下，未有逾陛下也。
units.en: Among the emperors of old who wore austerity on their own backs for the good of the realm, none has outdone you.
units.literal: Among emperors and kings of the past who personally practiced meagerness to benefit all under Heaven, none has exceeded Your Majesty.

units.zh: 然泰始開元以暨於今，十有五年矣。
units.en: Yet fifteen years have passed since the Taishi era began.
units.literal: Yet from the opening of Taishi down to the present, there are already fifteen years.

units.zh: 而軍國未豐，百姓不贍，一歲不登便有菜色者，誠由官眾事殷，復除猥濫，蠶食者多而親農者少也。
units.en: The army and the treasury are still poor, the people still lack reserves: a single bad harvest puts hunger in their faces. The reason is plain—too many officials, too many tasks, tax relief handed out indiscriminately, endless petty predators on the countryside, and too few hands actually at the plow.
units.literal: Yet the army and state are not abundant, the hundred surnames are not sufficient; if for one year the harvest does not ascend then there are those with vegetable color—truly it is because officials are many and affairs are pressing, exemptions are excessive and loose, those who nibble away are many while those who personally farm are few.

units.zh: 臣以頑疏，謬忝近職，每見聖詔以百姓饑饉為慮，無能雲補，伏用慚恧，敢不自竭，以對天問。
units.en: I am a dull man unworthy of a place near the throne, yet whenever I read your edicts' anguish over the people's hunger I burn with shame that I have offered no help worth mentioning; I can only pour out what little I know in answer to your question.
units.literal: Your subject, by dullness and roughness, wrongly is honored with a nearby post; whenever I see the sagely edict take the hundred surnames' hunger and famine as anxiety, unable to add even a cloud's worth of help, I prostrate in shame—yet I dare not fail to exhaust myself in answering Heaven's question.

units.zh: 舊都督有四，今並監軍，乃盈於十。
units.en: There used to be four regional commanders; with army supervisors added in, the number is now well over ten.
units.literal: Formerly area commanders were four; now together with army supervisors they exceed ten.

units.zh: 夏禹敷土，分為九州，今之刺史，幾向一倍。
units.en: Great Yu mapped the realm into nine provinces; we now maintain nearly twice as many provincial inspectors.
units.literal: Great Yu spread the soil and divided it into nine provinces; today's regional inspectors approach nearly double.

units.zh: 戶口比漢十分之一，而置郡縣更多。
units.en: Registered households are barely a tenth of what they were under the Han, yet we have more commanderies and counties than ever.
units.literal: Households and mouths are one-tenth compared to the Han, yet established commanderies and counties are more numerous.

units.zh: 空校牙門，無益宿衛，而虛立軍府，動有百數。
units.en: Idle posts clutter headquarters gates without strengthening the night watch, while empty army bureaus are opened by the hundred.
units.literal: Empty posts at headquarters gates bring no benefit to night guard, yet hollowly army offices are established—often reaching a hundred-odd.

units.zh: 五等諸侯，復坐置官屬。
units.en: The nobles of the five ranks sit in office while piling up personal staffs.
units.literal: The nobles of the five ranks again sit while appointing official subordinates.

units.zh: 諸所寵給，皆生於百姓。
units.en: Every one of those salaries is wrung from the common people.
units.literal: All that is lavishly granted is born from the hundred surnames.

units.zh: 一夫不農，有受其饑，今之不農，不可勝計。
units.en: If one man leaves the plow, someone goes hungry; today the number of men not farming is beyond counting.
units.literal: If one man does not farm, there is one who receives his hunger; of today's not farming, the number cannot be counted.

units.zh: 縱使五稼普收，僅足相接；
units.en: Even if every crop ripened well, the harvest would barely meet consumption;
units.literal: Even if the five grains were universally harvested, it would barely be enough to connect;

units.zh: 暫有災患，便不繼贍。
units.en: the slightest disaster breaks the chain of supply.
units.literal: Briefly if there is disaster or hardship, then it does not continue to provision.

units.zh: 以為當今之急，先並官省事，靜事息役，上下用心，惟農是務也。」
units.en: I therefore believe the most urgent task now is to merge offices, reduce redundant business, quiet lawsuits, and lighten corvée so that high and low alike devote their efforts solely to agriculture."
units.literal: Your subject holds that the urgency of the present is first to merge offices and cut affairs, still affairs and rest corvée, above and below apply their minds, and farming alone is the task.

units.zh: 咸在位多所執正。
units.en: In office Fu Xian repeatedly stood his ground on points of principle.
units.literal: Xian in office often upheld what was correct in many things.

units.zh: 豫州大中正夏侯駿上言，魯國小中正、司空司馬孔毓，四移病所，不能接賓，求以尚書郎曹馥代毓，旬日復上毓為中正。
units.en: Xiahou Jun, the grand rectifier for Yu province, reported that Kong Yu—minor rectifier for Lu and a staff major under the minister of works—had changed his sick-leave residence four times and could not receive visitors; he asked that Cao Fu, a gentleman of the secretariat, replace Kong Yu, then ten days later submitted Kong Yu's name again for the rectifier's post.
units.literal: The grand rectifier of Yu Province, Xiahou Jun, submitted a statement that Kong Yu, minor rectifier of Lu and a major to the minister of works, had shifted his sick residence four times and could not receive guests, requesting to replace Yu with Cao Fu, gentleman of the secretariat; after ten days he again submitted Yu as rectifier.

units.zh: 司徒三卻，駿故據正。
units.en: The minister of education rejected the nomination three times, but Xiahou Jun stubbornly insisted he was right.
units.literal: The minister of education thrice rejected; Jun therefore held to rectitude.

units.zh: 咸以駿與奪惟意，乃奏免駿大中正。
units.en: Fu Xian held that Xiahou Jun was making appointments and dismissals on whim, and memorialized to remove him as grand rectifier.
units.literal: Xian, because Jun's granting and taking away followed whim, then memorialized to dismiss Jun as grand rectifier.

units.zh: 司徒魏舒，駿之姻屬，屢卻不署，咸據正甚苦。
units.en: The minister of education, Wei Shu—related to Xiahou Jun by marriage—repeatedly refused to countersign; Fu Xian pressed his case with bitter persistence.
units.literal: Minister of Education Wei Shu, Jun's marriage-relative, repeatedly rejected and would not sign; Xian held to rectitude with great bitterness.

units.zh: 舒終不從，咸遂獨上。
units.en: Wei Shu still would not yield, so Fu Xian submitted his memorial alone.
units.literal: Shu in the end did not comply; Xian thereupon submitted alone.

units.zh: 舒奏咸激訕不直，詔轉咸為車騎司馬。
units.en: Wei Shu then accused Fu Xian of provocation and slander; the court transferred Fu Xian to the post of marshal in the chariots-and-cavalry command.
units.literal: Shu memorialized that Xian was provocative and slanderous and not straight; by edict Xian was transferred to be marshal of the chariots and cavalry.

units.zh: 咸以世俗奢侈，又上書曰：「臣以為穀帛難生，而用之不節，無緣不匱。
units.en: Distressed by the luxury of the age, Fu Xian sent up another memorial: "Grain and silk are hard to come by; if we spend them without restraint, they cannot fail to run short.
units.literal: Xian, because the customs of the age were extravagant, also submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject holds that grain and silk are hard to produce, and if they are used without restraint, there is no cause for them not to be exhausted.

units.zh: 故先王之化天下，食肉衣帛，皆有其制。
units.en: The kings of old who civilized the realm laid down clear rules even for such things as eating meat and wearing silk.
units.literal: Therefore former kings' transforming all under Heaven—eating meat and wearing silk—each had its regulation.

units.zh: 竊謂奢侈之費，甚於天災。
units.en: I would add that the waste of extravagance does more harm than flood or drought.
units.literal: Your subject privately holds that the expense of extravagance exceeds natural disaster.

units.zh: 古者堯有茅茨，今之百姓競豐其屋。
units.en: In Yao’s day the ruler lived under a thatched roof; today ordinary families compete to build ever grander houses.
units.literal: In antiquity Yao had thatched huts; the common people of today vie to make their houses lavish.

units.zh: 古者臣無玉食，今之賈豎皆厭粱肉。
units.en: Once, ministers did not dine off jade vessels; today even petty traders grow weary of the finest grain and meat.
units.literal: In antiquity ministers had no jade food; today’s merchant lads all are sated with fine millet and meat.

units.zh: 古者后妃乃有殊飾，今之婢妾被服綾羅。
units.en: Ornaments once reserved for queens and consorts now wrap maids and concubines in damask and gauze.
units.literal: In antiquity only empresses and consorts had special ornaments; today’s maids and concubines are clothed in gauze and thin silk.

units.zh: 古者大夫乃不徒行，今之賤隸乘輕驅肥。
units.en: Grandees alone once rode rather than walked; today the meanest servants clip along in light carriages behind sleek horses.
units.literal: In antiquity only grandees did not walk on foot; today’s base bondsmen ride light carriages and drive fat horses.

units.zh: 古者人稠地狹而有儲蓄，由於節也；
units.en: When population pressed on narrow land, people still saved—because they lived frugally;
units.literal: In antiquity people were dense and land narrow yet there were stores—this was because of restraint;

units.zh: 今者土廣人稀而患不足，由於奢也。
units.en: Now the realm is wide and thinly peopled, yet we fret over want—because we have grown extravagant.
units.literal: Today land is wide and people sparse yet we worry about insufficiency—this is because of extravagance.

units.zh: 欲時之儉，當詰其奢；
units.en: If you want the age to be thrifty, you must call its extravagance to account;
units.literal: To seek frugality for the age, one must investigate its extravagance;

units.zh: 奢不見詰，轉相高尚。
units.en: if extravagance goes unchallenged, people only egg one another on toward finer taste.
units.literal: If extravagance is not investigated, they turn and esteem one another ever more highly.

units.zh: 昔毛玠為吏部尚書，時無敢好衣美食者。
units.en: When Mao Jie headed the ministry of appointments, for a while no one dared flaunt fine dress or rich food.
units.literal: In the past when Mao Jie was director of the ministry of appointments, for a time none dared love fine clothes or good food.

units.zh: 魏武帝歎曰：『孤之法不如毛尚書。』
units.en: Cao Cao sighed, “My statutes do not match Director Mao’s standards.”
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei sighed: “My laws are not the equal of Director Mao.”

units.zh: 令使諸部用心，各如毛玠，風俗之移，在不難矣。」
units.en: If every bureau could apply itself as Mao Jie did, changing the temper of the times would not be hard."
units.literal: If we ordered every department to apply their minds each as Mao Jie did, shifting custom would not be difficult."

units.zh: 又議移縣獄於郡及二社應立，朝廷從之。
units.en: He also urged moving county jails to the commandery level and founding the paired altars of soil and grain; the court agreed.
units.literal: He also debated moving county prisons to the commandery and establishing the two altars of soil and grain; the court accepted.

units.zh: 遷尚書左丞。
units.en: He was promoted to left assistant director in the secretariat.
units.literal: He was promoted to left assistant in the secretariat.

units.zh: 惠帝即位，楊駿輔政。
units.en: When Emperor Hui came to the throne, Yang Jun directed the government as regent.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui mounted the throne, Yang Jun assisted the government.

units.zh: 咸言於駿曰：「事與世變，禮隨時宜，諒暗之不行尚矣。
units.en: Fu Xian said to Yang Jun: “Circumstances change with the times, and ritual must suit the moment; it has been clear for ages that the old palace mourning cannot be kept unchanged.
units.literal: Xian spoke to Jun, saying: “Affairs change with the age; ritual follows what fits the times; that mourning seclusion is not practiced has long been clear.

units.zh: 由世道彌薄，權不可假，故雖斬焉在疚，而躬覽萬機也。
units.en: The moral climate has thinned, and supreme authority cannot be handed off; that is why even a ruler in the deepest mourning still has to take up the myriad affairs of state himself.
units.literal: Because the Way of the world grows ever thinner, power cannot be lent away; therefore although one is cutting grief in deep mourning, yet one personally inspects the ten thousand threads of business.

units.zh: 逮至漢文，以天下體大，服重難久，遂制既葬而除。
units.en: Emperor Wen of Han, seeing the realm too vast for prolonged heavy mourning, decreed that mourning dress end with the burial.
units.literal: Down to Emperor Wen of Han, because the realm under Heaven was large in scale and heavy mourning could not be prolonged long, thereupon the rule was to remove mourning garments once burial was complete.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝雖大孝蒸蒸，亦從時釋服，制心喪三年，至於萬機之事，則有不遑。
units.en: Emperor Wu, our dynastic founder, was deeply filial, yet he too laid aside formal mourning when the times required it, keeping a three-year grief in his heart while knowing he could not neglect the myriad tasks of rule.
units.literal: Our founding emperor Emperor Wu, though his filial devotion was abundant, also followed the times in laying aside mourning garments, setting heart-mourning for three years; as for the ten thousand threads of business, then there was no leisure.

units.zh: 今聖上欲委政於公，諒暗自居，此雖謙讓之心，而天下未以為善。
units.en: The reigning emperor wishes to leave government in your hands while he withdraws in mourning; that may show modest intent, but the empire does not read it as wise.
units.literal: Now the sagely sovereign wishes to entrust government to your lordship and dwell in mourning seclusion himself—this, although a mind of yielding, is not what all under Heaven takes for good.

units.zh: 天下未以為善者，以億兆顒顒，戴仰宸極，聽於冢宰，懼天光有蔽。
units.en: People look up to the throne alone; if they hear that only the chief minister decides policy, they fear the sovereign’s light will be hidden.
units.literal: The reason all under Heaven does not take it for good is that the millions lift their heads, looking up to the pole star; hearing that the grand steward alone decides, they fear the heavenly light may be blocked.

units.zh: 人心既已若此，而明公處之固未為易也。
units.en: Hearts are already uneasy; for you, sir, the position cannot be an easy one.
units.literal: Human hearts are already like this, yet your lordship’s handling of it is surely not easy.

units.zh: 竊謂山陵之事既畢，明公當思隆替之宜。
units.en: Once the imperial burial is over, you must weigh what will strengthen the state and what will weaken it.
units.literal: Your subject privately holds that once matters on the hills and tombs are finished, your lordship ought to weigh what suits flourishing or decline.

units.zh: 周公聖人，猶不免謗。
units.en: Even the Duke of Zhou, a sage, could not escape slander.
units.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a sage, yet even he could not escape slander.

units.zh: 以此推之，周公之任既未易而處，況聖上春秋非成王之年乎！
units.en: If the Duke of Zhou’s burden was hard to bear, how much harder when our emperor is not a child like King Cheng of old!
units.literal: From this one infers: the Duke of Zhou’s burden was already not easy to bear—how much more when the sagely sovereign’s years do not match King Cheng’s!

units.zh: 得意忘言，言未易盡。
units.en: When the point is taken, words may cease; yet words can never say everything.
units.literal: When the meaning is grasped, words are forgotten; words are not easy to exhaust.

units.zh: 苟明公有以察其悾款，言豈在多。」
units.en: If you can see the earnest loyalty behind my bluntness, I need not say more.”
units.literal: If your lordship can see the sincerity in my earnest dullness, words need not be many.”

units.zh: 時司隸荀愷從兄喪，自表赴哀，詔聽之而未下，愷乃造駿。
units.en: Meanwhile Xun Kai, the colonel director of retainers, had petitioned to mourn a deceased cousin; the throne had granted leave but the edict had not yet been issued when Kai went to Yang Jun’s house.
units.literal: At that time the colonel director of retainers Xun Kai, on a cousin’s death, personally memorialized to go to mourning; an edict had approved it but not yet been issued, yet Kai went to Jun’s place.

units.zh: 咸因奏曰：「死喪之戚，兄弟孔懷。
units.en: Fu Xian seized on this and memorialized: “The grief of death strikes brothers most keenly.
units.literal: Xian thereupon memorialized: “The grief of death: brothers greatly cherish one another.

units.zh: 同堂亡隕，方在信宿，聖恩矜憫，聽使臨喪。
units.en: A cousin has just died; barely two nights have passed. The court in its mercy would let him attend the rites.
units.literal: A hall-mate has died and fallen; we are still within two nights; the sagely grace pities and allows attendance at mourning.

units.zh: 詔未下而便以行造，急諂媚之敬，無友于之情。
units.en: To hurry to a private visit before the edict appears is eager flattery, not the affection due between brothers.
units.literal: The edict had not been issued yet he used motion to go pay visit—hasty flattery’s reverence, no fraternal feeling toward friends.

units.zh: 宜加顯貶，以隆風教。」
units.en: He should be publicly demoted to uphold public morals.”
units.literal: He ought plainly to be demoted to thicken customs and teaching.”

units.zh: 帝以駿管朝政，有詔不問，駿甚憚之。
units.en: The emperor, because Yang Jun ran the government, ordered the charge dropped; Jun nonetheless came to fear Fu Xian deeply.
units.literal: The emperor, because Jun controlled court government, issued an edict not to pursue the matter; Jun greatly feared him.

units.zh: 咸復與駿箋諷切之，駿意稍折，漸以不平。
units.en: Fu Xian wrote again to needle Yang Jun; Jun yielded a little on the surface but grew quietly resentful.
units.literal: Xian again wrote Jun a letter exhorting him incisively; Jun’s intent bent slightly but gradually turned resentful.

units.zh: 由是欲出為京兆、弘農太守，駿甥李斌說駿，不宜斥出正人，乃止。
units.en: Jun then planned to send Fu Xian out as governor of Jingzhao or Hongnong, but Li Bin, Jun’s nephew, argued that an upright man should not be banished from the capital, and Jun dropped the idea.
units.literal: Thereupon [Jun] wished to send [Xian] out as governor of Jingzhao or Hongnong; Jun’s nephew Li Bin persuaded Jun that one should not expel an upright man, and so it stopped.

units.zh: 駿弟濟素與咸善，與咸書曰：「江海之流混混，故能成其深廣也。
units.en: Yang Ji, Jun’s younger brother, who was friendly with Fu Xian, wrote: “Rivers and seas run broad and muddy, and that is how they grow deep and wide.
units.literal: Jun’s younger brother Ji had always been on good terms with Xian; he wrote to Xian: “River and sea currents are turbid and vast, therefore they can achieve depth and breadth.

units.zh: 天下大器，非可稍了，而相觀每事欲了。
units.en: The empire is no trifle to be ticked off in pieces, yet you try to finish every matter at a glance.
units.literal: The great vessel of all under Heaven cannot be grasped in little bits; yet you inspect everything wishing to get it all done.

units.zh: 生子癡，了官事，官事未易了也。
units.en: The proverb runs, “Raise a dull son, leave him office work”—office work is never really finished.
units.literal: Have a dull son and set him to finishing official business—official business is not easy to finish.

units.zh: 了事正作癡，復為快耳！
units.en: To “finish” business is to play the fool, yet people call that clever!
units.literal: Finishing affairs is precisely making foolishness, yet we call it sharp!

units.zh: 左丞總司天臺，維正八坐，此未易居。
units.en: The left assistant steers the high ministries and keeps the eight senior seats in line—that is no easy seat.
units.literal: The left assistant oversees the celestial terrace and aligns the eight seats—this is not an easy place to stand.

units.zh: 以君盡性而處未易居之任，益不易也。
units.en: For a man of your uncompromising nature to hold such a post is harder still.
units.literal: That you, with full nature, occupy a place not easy to stand—that is even less easy.

units.zh: 想慮破頭，故具有白。」
units.en: I worry until my head aches, so I spell it all out here.”
units.literal: My thoughts worry until they break my head; therefore I write this in full.”

units.zh: 咸答曰：「衛公云酒色之殺人，此甚於作直。
units.en: Fu Xian answered: “Lord Wei says wine and lust kill more surely than blunt honesty.
units.literal: Xian replied: “Lord Wei says wine and sex kill people—this is worse than acting straight.

units.zh: 坐酒色死，人不為悔。
units.en: Men die of drink and lust without a twinge of regret.
units.literal: Dying through wine and sex, people do not regret it.

units.zh: 逆畏以直致禍，此由心不直正，欲以苟且為明哲耳！
units.en: To shun disaster by silence shows a heart that is not straight—it is cowardice dressed up as wisdom.
units.literal: Contrariwise fearing that straightness brings disaster—that is because the heart is not straight and upright, wishing to take evasive compromise as wise clarity!

units.zh: 自古以直致禍者，當自矯枉過直，或不忠允，欲以亢厲為聲，故致忿耳。
units.en: Those who court ruin by bluntness usually overcorrect, or lack true loyalty, or play the martyr for fame—and so they earn resentment.
units.literal: From antiquity those who brought disaster on themselves by straightness were either bending the straight too far, or not being loyal and sincere, wishing to borrow harshness for reputation, therefore incurring resentment.

units.zh: 安有空空為忠益，而當見疾乎！」
units.en: Would plain loyalty for the public good alone earn hatred?”
units.literal: How could blandly being loyal and beneficial then meet with jealousy!”

units.zh: 居無何，駿誅。
units.en: Soon afterward Yang Jun was executed.
units.literal: Before long, Jun was executed.

units.zh: 咸轉為太子中庶子，遷御史中丞。
units.en: Fu Xian was moved to palace attendant to the heir apparent, then promoted to metropolitan censor.
units.literal: Xian was transferred to palace subordinate to the heir apparent, then promoted metropolitan censor.

units.zh: 時太宰、汝南王亮輔政，咸致書曰：咸以為太甲、成王年在蒙幼，故有伊、周之事。
units.en: When the grand preceptor, Sima Liang, king of Runan, directed policy, Fu Xian wrote to him: I hold that Tai Jia and King Cheng were still in their minority, and therefore there occurred the regencies of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.
units.literal: When the grand preceptor, the king of Runan, Liang, directed the government, Xian sent a letter saying: Xian holds that Tai Jia and King Cheng, in years still tenderly young, therefore had the acts of Yi and Zhou.

units.zh: 聖人且猶不免疑，況臣既不聖，王非孺子，而可以行伊、周之事乎！
units.en: Even sages could not escape suspicion in such cases; how much less can I, no sage, claim the regency of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou when the king is no child!
units.literal: Even sages could not avoid suspicion—how much more when your subject is not a sage and the king is no child, yet one could perform the acts of Yi and Zhou!

units.zh: 上在諒暗，聽於冢宰，而楊駿無狀，便作伊、周，自為居天下之安，所以至死。
units.en: The emperor was in mourning seclusion and entrusted affairs to the chief steward, yet Yang Jun, utterly without propriety, cast himself as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, imagining he could hold the realm secure—and that is why he met his death.
units.literal: The sovereign was in mourning seclusion and listened to the chief steward, yet Yang Jun, lacking all propriety, at once played Yi and Zhou, thinking himself secure in possession of all under Heaven—this is why he died.

units.zh: 其罪既不可勝，亦是殿下所見。
units.en: His crimes were beyond counting, as Your Highness yourself witnessed.
units.literal: His crimes were already beyond numbering, as Your Highness also saw.

units.zh: 駿之見討，發自天聰，孟觀、李肇與知密旨耳。
units.en: Yang Jun's execution came from the emperor's own decision; only Meng Guan and Li Zhao knew the secret orders.
units.literal: Jun's being punished issued from Heaven's discernment; Meng Guan and Li Zhao alone shared knowledge of the secret intent.

units.zh: 至於論功，當歸美於上。
units.en: When merit is assessed, the credit should go to the throne.
units.literal: As for discussing merit, credit ought to be returned in praise to the sovereign.

units.zh: 觀等已數千戶縣侯，聖上以駿死莫不欣悅，故論功寧厚，以敘其歡心。
units.en: Guan and the others were already county marquises with estates of several thousand households. Since all rejoiced at Yang Jun's death, the emperor was willing to be generous in rewarding merit so as to share in that joy.
units.literal: Guan and the others were already county marquises of several thousand households; the sage sovereign, since none failed to rejoice at Jun's death, therefore in assessing merit would rather be generous, so as to express their glad hearts.

units.zh: 此群下所宜以實裁量，而遂扇動，東安封王，孟、李郡公，余侯伯子男，既妄有加，復又三等超遷。
units.en: Subordinates should have measured rewards by actual merit, yet agitation followed: the Lord of Dong'an was enfeoffed as a prince, Meng and Li as commandery dukes, and the rest as marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons—first granted without warrant, then promoted three ranks beyond measure.
units.literal: This is what the host of subordinates ought to measure by reality, yet they stirred things up: the Lord of Dong'an was enfeoffed as a king, Meng and Li as commandery dukes, the rest as marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons—first granted rashly, then promoted three ranks beyond measure.

units.zh: 此之熏赫，震動天地，自古以來，封賞未有若此者也。
units.en: Such dazzling rewards shook Heaven and Earth; never in history had enfeoffment and reward reached such heights.
units.literal: Such blazing splendor shook Heaven and Earth; from antiquity to the present, enfeoffments and rewards have never been like this.

units.zh: 無功而厚賞，莫不樂國有禍，禍起當復有大功也。
units.en: When men are richly rewarded without merit, all come to hope for national calamity, since calamity would bring fresh chances for great reward.
units.literal: Rewarding generously without merit—none failed to rejoice that the state would have disaster, for when disaster arose there would again be great merit.

units.zh: 人而樂禍，其可極乎！
units.en: When men rejoice in disaster, where will it end!
units.literal: If men rejoice in disaster, can it have a limit!

units.zh: 作此者，皆由東安公。
units.en: All of this was the work of the Lord of Dong'an.
units.literal: Those who did this all came through the Lord of Dong'an.

units.zh: 謂殿下至止，當有以正之。
units.en: When Your Highness takes charge, you should set this right.
units.literal: I say that when Your Highness arrives and stops, there ought to be means to set it right.

units.zh: 正之以道，眾亦何所怒乎！
units.en: Set it right by proper principle, and what cause would the multitude have for anger!
units.literal: If it is set right by the Way, what would the multitude have to resent!

units.zh: 眾之所怒，在於不平耳。
units.en: The multitude's anger rests on unfairness alone.
units.literal: What the multitude resents lies in unfairness alone.

units.zh: 而今皆更倍論，莫不失望。
units.en: Yet now rewards are reckoned at double measure, and all have lost hope.
units.literal: Yet now all are again counted at double measure, and none failed to lose hope.

units.zh: 咸之愚冗，不惟失望而已，竊以為憂。
units.en: In my dull incompetence I am not merely disappointed; I am privately deeply worried.
units.literal: Xian's stupidity and redundancy is not only disappointment; I privately hold it a matter for worry.

units.zh: 又討駿之時，殿下在外，實所不綜。
units.en: Moreover, when Yang Jun was punished, Your Highness was away and in truth had no part in directing it.
units.literal: Further, at the time of punishing Jun, Your Highness was outside and in truth did not oversee it.

units.zh: 今欲委重，故令殿下論功。
units.en: Now that weighty authority is to be entrusted to you, they have made Your Highness assess merit.
units.literal: Now wishing to entrust weighty matters, they therefore have Your Highness assess merit.

units.zh: 論功之事，實未易可處，莫若坐觀得失，有居正之事宜也。
units.en: Assessing merit is truly no easy task. Better to watch how things turn out and intervene only when a matter of right principle requires it.
units.literal: The matter of assessing merit is in truth not easy to handle; better to sit and observe gains and losses, and when there are matters of upright standing, then act.

units.zh: 咸復以亮輔政專權，又諫曰：「楊駿有震主之威，委任親戚，此天下所以喧嘩。
