units.en: Fu Xian, seeing that Sima Liang monopolized power as regent, remonstrated again: “Yang Jun’s authority overshadowed the throne and he packed office with kin—that is why the realm erupted in protest.
units.literal: Xian again, because Liang directed the government and monopolized power, remonstrated: “Yang Jun had awe that shook the ruler, delegating trust to kinsmen—that is why all under Heaven clamored.

units.zh: 今之處重，宜反此失。
units.en: Men who hold great power now should undo that mistake.
units.literal: Those who now stand in weight ought to reverse this fault.

units.zh: 謂宜靜默頤神，有大得失，乃維持之；
units.en: You should stay quiet, husband your strength, and intervene only on great issues of right and wrong;
units.literal: I say one ought to keep still, nurture spirit, and only for great gains or losses then uphold them;

units.zh: 自非大事，一皆抑遣。
units.en: everything short of that should be checked and turned aside.
units.literal: Whatever is not a great matter should altogether be checked and sent back.

units.zh: 比四造詣，及經過尊門，冠蓋車馬，填塞街衢，此之翕習，既宜弭息。
units.en: Four times lately I have called on you, and each time your gate was choked with carriages and riders; this ostentatious traffic ought to stop.
units.literal: Recently I have called on you four times, and passing your honored gate, caps and covers, carriages and horses fill and block the streets—this swelling bustle ought at once to be quelled.

units.zh: 又夏侯長容奉使為先帝請命，祈禱無感，先帝崩背，宜自咎責，而自求請命之勞，而公以為少府。
units.en: Moreover Xiahou Changrong was sent to pray for the late emperor’s life; the prayers failed; when the emperor died he should have blamed himself, yet he boasted of his mission’s hardship, and you, sir, made him minister of the household.
units.literal: Further, Xiahou Changrong went on mission to seek life for the late emperor; the prayers were without response; when the late emperor passed away, he ought to have blamed himself, yet he seeks credit for the toil of requesting life—yet your lordship made him minister of the household.

units.zh: 私竊之論，雲長容則公之姻，故至於此。
units.en: Whispered opinion says Changrong is your kinsman by marriage, which explains the appointment.
units.literal: Private gossip says that Changrong is your lordship’s in-law, and therefore it came to this.

units.zh: 一犬吠形，群犬吠聲，懼於群吠，遂至叵聽也。
units.en: One dog barks at a shadow and the pack joins in; fear that chorus and rumor becomes unbearable.
units.literal: One dog barks at a shape, the pack barks at the sound; fearing the pack’s barking, it becomes unbearable to listen.

units.zh: 咸之為人，不能面從而有後言。
units.en: I am not the sort to nod assent to your face and murmur behind your back.
units.literal: As for Xian’s person, he cannot consent to people’s faces yet later speak otherwise.

units.zh: 嘗觸楊駿，幾為身禍；
units.en: I once crossed Yang Jun and nearly lost my life;
units.literal: I once offended Yang Jun and nearly brought bodily disaster on myself;

units.zh: 況于殿下，而當有惜！
units.en: how much less would I hold back with you, Your Highness!
units.literal: how much more toward Your Highness—yet should there be reluctance!

units.zh: 往從駕，殿下見語：『卿不識韓非逆鱗之言耶，而欻摩天子逆鱗！』
units.en: Once, when I attended you on an outing, you said, “Have you not read Han Fei on the ruler’s ‘reverse scales’—yet you keep brushing the emperor’s!”
units.literal: Formerly, following the imperial carriage, Your Highness said to me: “Do you not know Han Fei’s words on contrary scales—yet you hastily rub the Son of Heaven’s contrary scales!”

units.zh: 自知所陳，誠𬱃𬱃觸猛獸之須耳。
units.en: I knew my words were timidly tugging the tiger’s whiskers.
units.literal: I knew that what I stated was truly timidly rubbing the fierce beast’s whiskers.

units.zh: 所以敢言，庶殿下當識其不勝區區。
units.en: I speak because I hope you will see how much earnest loyalty compels me.
units.literal: The reason I dare to speak is that I hope Your Highness will recognize that I cannot bear but to be utterly sincere.

units.zh: 前摩天子逆鱗，欲以盡忠；
units.en: When I pressed the late emperor it was to exhaust my loyalty;
units.literal: Formerly rubbing the Son of Heaven’s contrary scales was in order to exhaust loyalty;

units.zh: 今觸猛獸之須，非欲為惡，必將以此見恕。」
units.en: now I tug the tiger’s whiskers not from malice but in the trust that you will forgive me.”
units.literal: now touching the fierce beast’s whiskers is not wishing to do evil—it is certain that I will therefore be forgiven.”

units.zh: 亮不納。
units.en: Sima Liang ignored the advice.
units.literal: Liang did not accept.

units.zh: 長容者，夏侯駿也。
units.en: “Changrong” is the style name of Xiahou Jun.
units.literal: Changrong is Xiahou Jun.

units.zh: 會丙寅，詔群僚舉郡縣之職以補內官。
units.en: On a bingyin day the court ordered officials to nominate local posts to fill vacancies at the capital.
units.literal: On the bingyin day, an edict ordered the host of officials to recommend commandery and county posts to fill inner offices.

units.zh: 咸復上書曰：臣咸以為夫興化之要，在於官人。
units.en: Fu Xian submitted another memorial: "Your subject Xian holds that the key to fostering moral transformation lies in appointing the right men to office."
units.literal: Xian again submitted a memorial saying: Your subject Xian holds that the essential of fostering transformation lies in putting men in office.

units.zh: 才非一流，職有不同。
units.en: Talents are not all of one kind, and offices differ in their demands.
units.literal: Talents are not of one stream; duties have their differences.

units.zh: 譬諸林木，洪纖枉直，各有攸施。
units.en: Compare them to trees in a forest: large and small, bent and straight, each has its proper use.
units.literal: Compare them to trees in a forest: large and small, bent and straight, each has its proper use.

units.zh: 故明揚逮於仄陋，疇咨無拘內外。
units.en: Therefore the worthy are elevated even from humble and obscure places, and consultation in choosing men knows no boundary between inner and outer circles.
units.literal: Therefore the bright are raised even from narrow and lowly places, and consultation in choosing men is not confined to inner or outer circles.

units.zh: 內外之任，出處隨宜，中間選用，惟內是隆。
units.en: Inner and outer posts should be filled as each case requires, yet in practice selection favors the inner service alone.
units.literal: Inner and outer duties, entering office or leaving it as each case suits—yet in selection between them, only the inner is exalted.

units.zh: 外舉既穨，復多節目，競內薄外，遂成風俗。
units.en: Outer recommendation has already declined, and multiplying regulations have bred a custom of favoring inner appointments and slighting the outer service.
units.literal: Outer recommendation having already declined, there are moreover many rules and items; competing to favor the inner and slight the outer, it has become custom.

units.zh: 此弊誠宜亟革之，當內外通塞無所偏耳。
units.en: This abuse should be reformed at once; inner and outer appointments should be treated without partiality.
units.literal: This abuse truly ought urgently to be reformed; inner and outer should be open or closed with no partiality.

units.zh: 既使通塞無偏，若選用不平，有以深責，責之苟深，無憂不平也。
units.en: Once inner and outer posts are treated without bias, unfair appointments can be met with stern accountability; where accountability is strict, unfairness need not be feared.
units.literal: Once open and closed are without partiality, if selection and employment are not fair, there are means to hold men deeply accountable; if accountability is truly deep, there is no worry about unfairness.

units.zh: 且膠柱不可以調瑟，況乎官人而可以限乎！
units.en: A peg glued in place cannot tune a zither; how much less can the appointment of officials be bound by rigid limits!
units.literal: Moreover, gluing the pegs makes it impossible to tune the zither—how much more can men in office be constrained by limits!

units.zh: 伏思所限者，以防選用不能出人。
units.en: I understand that limits were imposed to keep selection from failing to produce outstanding men.
units.literal: I reflect that what is limited is meant to guard against selection and employment failing to produce outstanding men.

units.zh: 不能出人，當隨事而制，無須限法。
units.en: When outstanding men are not produced, measures should be adapted to the case; there is no need for rigid statutory limits.
units.literal: If outstanding men are not produced, one ought to regulate according to the matter; there is no need for limiting laws.

units.zh: 法之有限，其於致遠，無乃泥乎！
units.en: Statutory limits, when one aims at lasting success, become mere obstruction!
units.literal: Where law has limits, for reaching far, is it not merely obstructive!

units.zh: 或謂不制其法，以何為貴？
units.en: Some ask: if the law is not regulated, what will keep selection honorable?
units.literal: Some say that if its law is not regulated, by what is it to be honored?

units.zh: 臣聞刑懲小人，義責君子，君子之責，在心不在限也。
units.en: I have heard that punishments chastise petty men while righteousness holds gentlemen accountable; a gentleman's accountability rests in the heart, not in statutory limits.
units.literal: Your subject has heard that punishments chastise petty men, while righteousness holds gentlemen accountable; the gentleman's accountability lies in the heart, not in limits.

units.zh: 正始中，任何晏以選舉，內外之眾職各得其才，粲然之美于斯可觀。
units.en: In the Zhengshi era, when He Yan was charged with selection, every post inner and outer received the right man, and the brilliance of that achievement was plain for all to see.
units.literal: In the Zhengshi era, when He Yan was charged with selection, the many posts inner and outer each obtained its man, and the bright beauty thereof could be seen in this.

units.zh: 如此，非徒禦之以限，法之所致，乃委任之由也。
units.en: This success came not from warding off abuse by limits alone but from the basis of true entrustment and appointment.
units.literal: Like this—it was not merely defended by limits; what the law achieved came from the basis of entrustment and appointment.

units.zh: 委任之懼，甚於限法。
units.en: The fear that comes with real entrustment is greater than any fear of statutory limits.
units.literal: The fear that comes with entrustment is greater than limiting law.

units.zh: 是法之失，非己之尤，尤不在己，責之無懼，所謂『齊之以刑，人免而無恥』者也。
units.en: When the law fails, it is not one's own fault; if the fault is not one's own, accountability holds no terror—this is what is meant by "regulate them by punishments, and the people avoid wrong but feel no shame."
units.literal: When the law fails, it is not one's own fault; if the fault is not in oneself, in being held accountable there is no fear—this is what is called "regulate them by punishments, and the people avoid wrong but are without shame."

units.zh: 苟委任之，一則慮罪之及，二則懼致怨謗。
units.en: When one is truly entrusted with selection, one first fears punishment and second fears incurring resentment and slander.
units.literal: If one is truly entrusted, first one fears that punishment will reach one, second one fears incurring resentment and slander.

units.zh: 己快則朝野稱詠，不善則眾惡見歸，此之戰戰，孰與倚限法以苟免乎！
units.en: Success brings praise from court and countryside alike; failure brings public hatred upon one's head. Such trembling caution—how can it compare with leaning on statutory limits merely to escape blame!
units.literal: If one succeeds, court and countryside sing one's praise; if one does ill, the multitude's hatred falls upon one—such trembling caution, how does it compare with leaning on limiting law to seek mere escape!

units.zh: 咸再為本郡中正，遭繼母憂去官。
units.en: Fu Xian twice served as grand rectifier for his home commandery; he resigned to mourn his stepmother.
units.literal: Xian twice was rectifier for his native commandery; on encountering his stepmother’s bereavement he left office.

units.zh: 頃之，起以議郎，長兼司隸校尉。
units.en: Soon he was recalled as a gentleman consultant and acting colonel director of retainers.
units.literal: Before long he was raised up as discussion gentleman, acting concurrently as colonel director of retainers.

units.zh: 咸前後固辭，不聽，敕使者就拜，咸復送還印綬。
units.en: He declined repeatedly; the court ignored him, sent envoys to invest him in office, and he returned the seal and ribbon again.
units.literal: Xian repeatedly and firmly declined and was not listened to; the emperor ordered envoys to go invest him, and Xian again sent back the seal and cord.

units.zh: 公車不通，催使攝職。
units.en: The petition channel was blocked while the court pressed him to assume the post.
units.literal: The public carriage channel was blocked; they pressed him to take up duty.

units.zh: 咸以身無兄弟，喪祭無主，重自陳乞，乃使於官舍設靈坐。
units.en: Because he had no brothers to preside over the rites, he pleaded again at length and was allowed to set up a mourning altar in his official quarters.
units.literal: Xian, because he personally had no brothers and for mourning and sacrifice had no master, heavily stated his plea again; thereupon he was allowed to set up a spirit seat in the official residence.

units.zh: 咸又上表曰：「臣既駑弱，不勝重任。
units.en: He submitted another memorial: “I am a dull, feeble man unfit for a heavy charge.
units.literal: Xian again submitted a table saying: “Your subject is both blunt and weak, and cannot bear a heavy charge.

units.zh: 加在哀疚，假息日闋，陛下過意，授非所堪。
units.en: Grief has worn me down day by day; Your Majesty overestimates me and gives me duties I cannot sustain.
units.literal: Added to mourning grief, borrowed breath daily wanes; Your Majesty over-favors me and appoints me to what I cannot sustain.

units.zh: 披露丹款，歸窮上聞，謬詔既往，終然無改。
units.en: I have laid my heart bare and sent my plea to the throne; mistaken edicts went out and nothing was changed.
units.literal: I have laid bare my crimson sincerity and returned my plea to your ear above; wrongly issued edicts have gone out, yet in the end there is no change.

units.zh: 臣雖不能滅身以全禮教，義無靦然，虛忝隆寵。
units.en: Though I cannot die to vindicate ritual, I cannot in good conscience accept empty honors.
units.literal: Though your subject cannot destroy his person to preserve ritual instruction, in principle there is no way to face it vainly and dishonor excessive favor.

units.zh: 前受嚴詔，視事之日，私心自誓，隕越為報。
units.en: When I took office under your stern order I swore I would give my life in return.
units.literal: Earlier I received a stern edict; on the day I took up affairs I swore privately that I would dash myself to pieces in repayment.

units.zh: 以貨賂流行，所宜深絕，切敕都官，以此為先。
units.en: Bribery was rampant and had to be stopped; I ordered the capital bureaus to strike at it first.
units.literal: Bribery flows and spreads—this ought to be drastically cut off; I urgently charged the capital officials to take this as first priority.

units.zh: 而經彌日月，未有所得。
units.en: Months have passed and nothing has come of it.
units.literal: Yet months have passed and nothing has been obtained.

units.zh: 斯由陛下有以獎厲，慮於愚戇，將必死系，故自掩檢以避其鋒耳。
units.en: Your Majesty’s rewards encourage them to think that blunt honesty ends in prison or death, so they hide and lie low to dodge the blow.
units.literal: This is because Your Majesty has ways to reward and spur them, and they expect that dull fidelity will surely end in death or bonds, therefore they cover and inspect themselves to avoid the edge.

units.zh: 在職有日，既無赫然之舉，又不應弦垂翅，人誰復憚？
units.en: I have been in office some days, yet I have made no striking move, nor have I made wings droop at the twang of a bowstring; who then will fear me?
units.literal: In office for days, neither having any striking achievement nor like a bowstring snapping a wing—who will again fear?

units.zh: 故光祿大夫劉毅為司隸，聲震內外，遠近清肅。
units.en: When Liu Yi held this post, his name shook the capital and the regions grew orderly.
units.literal: Therefore Grand Counsellor Liu Yi, as colonel director of retainers, his reputation shook within and without, near and far were pure and austere.

units.zh: 非徒毅有王臣匪躬之節，亦由所奏見從，威風得伸也。」
units.en: It was not only Liu Yi’s selfless integrity—the throne also backed his memorials, so his authority could bite.”
units.literal: It was not only that Yi had the integrity of a royal minister who is not for himself—also because what he memorialized was followed, and his awe-inspiring wind could extend.”

units.zh: 詔曰：「但當思必應繩中理，威風日伸，何獨劉毅！」
units.en: The edict answered: “See that every case you measure against principle; your authority will grow daily—why cite Liu Yi alone?”
units.literal: The edict said: “Only consider applying the cord to what truly hits principle—day by day your awe-inspiring wind will extend; why only Liu Yi!”

units.zh: 時朝廷寬弛，豪右放恣，交私請托，朝野溷淆。
units.en: The court had grown lax; great families traded private favors until court and countryside were a blur.
units.literal: At that time the court was lax and slack; powerful magnates gave free rein, mingling private requests and entrustments; court and countryside were confused.

units.zh: 咸奏免河南尹澹、左將軍倩、廷尉高光、兼河南尹何攀等，京都肅然，貴戚懾伏。
units.en: Fu Xian impeached the governor of Henan (surnamed Dan), the general of the left (surnamed Qian), the commandant of justice Gao Guang, and the concurrent governor of Henan He Pan; the capital grew orderly and the great houses trembled.
units.literal: Xian memorialized to dismiss the governor of Henan, Dan, the general of the left, Qian, the commandant of justice Gao Guang, concurrent governor of Henan He Pan, and others; the capital was austere, and noble in-laws were awed into submission.

units.zh: 咸以「聖人久于其道，天下化成。
units.en: Fu Xian quoted: “When the sage long pursues his course, the realm is shaped by it.
units.literal: Xian cited: “When the sage is long on his way, all under Heaven is transformed and completed.

units.zh: 是以唐、虞三載考績，九年黜陟。
units.en: Thus under Tang and Yu officials were graded every three years and promoted or demoted over nine.
units.literal: Therefore Tang and Yu examined achievements over three years, promoting and demoting over nine years.

units.zh: 其在《周禮》，三年大比。
units.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribes a great review every three years.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, there is the great comparison every three years.

units.zh: 孔子亦云，『三年有成』。
units.en: Confucius too said, “Give three years and there will be results.”
units.literal: Confucius also said, “In three years there is accomplishment.”

units.zh: 而中間以來，長吏到官，未幾便遷，百姓困于無定，吏卒疲於送迎」。
units.en: Yet of late magistrates are shuffled after a short stay; the people suffer endless instability, and runners collapse escorting one chief after another.”
units.literal: Yet in the middle period since then, when senior officers reach their post, before long they are transferred; the hundred surnames are worn out by having no stability, clerks and soldiers exhausted by seeing off and welcoming.”

units.zh: 時僕射王戎兼吏部，咸奏：「戎備位臺輔，兼掌選舉，不能謐靜風俗，以凝庶績，至令人心傾動，開張浮競。
units.en: Vice-director Wang Rong then ran the ministry of appointments; Fu Xian charged: “Rong sits among the chief ministers and holds appointments, yet he cannot steady custom or settle administration; hearts waver and empty rivalry spreads.
units.literal: At that time the vice-director Wang Rong concurrently held the ministry of appointments; Xian memorialized: “Rong occupies a place among ministerial supports and concurrently controls selection; he cannot calm custom and stillness, to coalesce the duties of the many—to the point of letting human hearts tilt and drift, opening and spreading empty rivalry.

units.zh: 中郎李重、李義不相匡正。
units.en: The gentleman-attendants Li Chong and Li Yi never correct him.
units.literal: The gentleman-attendants Li Chong and Li Yi do not correct him.

units.zh: 請免戎等官。」
units.en: I ask that Wang Rong and his like be removed from office.”
units.literal: I ask that Rong and others be dismissed from office.”

units.zh: 詔曰：「政道之本，誠宜久於其職，咸奏是也。
units.en: The edict said: “Long tenure is the root of good government; Fu Xian is right.
units.literal: The edict said: “The root of governing the way truly lies in long tenure in one’s post; what Xian memorialized is right.

units.zh: 戎職在論道，吾所崇委，其解禁止。」
units.en: Wang Rong’s duty is to counsel on the Way, which I value; lift the restrictions on him.”
units.literal: Rong’s duty lies in discussing the Way—I esteem and entrust him; as for him, dissolve the prohibition.”

units.zh: 御史中丞解結以咸劾戎為違典制，越局侵官，干非其分，奏免咸官。
units.en: Metropolitan censor Xie Jie argued that impeaching Wang Rong broke the rules, overstepped Fu Xian’s charge, and meddled beyond his rank; he asked that Fu Xian be dismissed.
units.literal: Metropolitan Censor Xie Jie held that Xian’s impeachment of Rong violated canonical regulation, overstepped his office and encroached on another’s duty, meddling beyond his portion, and memorialized to dismiss Xian from office.

units.zh: 詔亦不許。
units.en: The throne again refused.
units.literal: An edict again did not permit it.

units.zh: 咸上事以為「按令，御史中丞督司百僚。
units.en: Fu Xian argued in a memorial: "By statute the metropolitan censor supervises every official at court.
units.literal: Xian submitted a memorial holding: "According to the ordinance, the metropolitan censor supervises the hundred officials.

units.zh: 皇太子以下，其在行馬內，有違法憲者皆彈糾之。
units.en: Everyone from the crown prince downward who breaks the law inside the imperial patrol corridor falls under his impeachment.
units.literal: Below the crown prince, those within the mounted patrol corridor who violate statutes are all impeached and investigated.

units.zh: 雖在行馬外，而監司不糾，亦得奏之。
units.en: Even outside that corridor, if the regional inspectors fail to act, he may still memorialize against them.
units.literal: Although outside the mounted corridor, if supervising officials do not impeach, he may still memorialize on them.

units.zh: 如令之文，行馬之內有違法憲，謂禁防之事耳。
units.en: The statute’s wording ties the corridor to palace security alone.
units.literal: As the ordinance's wording stands, violations of statutes within the mounted corridor refer to matters of forbidden-precinct security alone.

units.zh: 宮內禁防，外司不得而行，故專施中丞。
units.en: Inner-palace security is closed to outside bureaus, which is why the metropolitan censor alone holds that beat.
units.literal: Forbidden precincts inside the palace—outside agencies may not act therein—therefore authority is vested solely in the central censor.

units.zh: 今道路橋梁不修，鬥訟屠沽不絕，如此之比，中丞推責州坐，即今所謂行馬內語施於禁防。
units.en: Neglected roads, endless lawsuits, unruly markets—the censor blames the province, yet people now stretch the phrase ‘inside the corridor’ to cover such civic ills.
units.literal: Now roads and bridges are not repaired, brawls and butchers and peddlers do not cease—such cases: the censor presses blame on the province to sit—then what is now called 'within the mounted corridor' language is applied to security matters.

units.zh: 既雲中丞督司百僚矣，何復說行馬之內乎！
units.en: If the censor already oversees all officials, why narrow him again to the corridor?
units.literal: Since it already says the central censor supervises the hundred officials, why again speak of 'within the mounted corridor'!

units.zh: 既雲百僚，而不得復說行馬之內者，內外眾官謂之百僚，則通內外矣。
units.en: The ‘hundred officials’ means everyone at court and in the provinces—inside and outside together.
units.literal: Since it says 'hundred officials,' yet may not again speak of 'within the mounted corridor'—the many officials inside and out are called the hundred officials, then it comprehends inside and outside.

units.zh: 司隸所以不復說行馬內外者，禁防之事已於中丞說之故也。
units.en: The colonel director omits the corridor because the censor’s statute already covers palace security.
units.literal: The reason the colonel director of retainers does not again speak of inside or outside the mounted corridor is that security matters were already stated with regard to the central censor.

units.zh: 中丞、司隸俱糾皇太子以下，則共對司內外矣，不為中丞專司內百僚，司隸專司外百僚。
units.en: Censor and colonel both impeach from the crown prince down; they share inner and outer duty—it is not a split between two separate rosters.
units.literal: Central censor and colonel director of retainers together impeach from the crown prince downward, then they jointly face duties inside and outside—it is not that the central censor solely supervises inner hundred officials and the colonel solely outer hundred officials.

units.zh: 自有中丞、司隸以來，更互奏內外眾官，惟所糾得無內外之限也。
units.en: Since both offices were created they have taken turns impeaching officials everywhere, with no hard line between inner and outer.
units.literal: From the time there have been central censor and colonel director of retainers, they have alternately memorialized on many officials inside and out—only when impeaching there is no inside-outside limit.

units.zh: 而結一旦橫挫臣，臣前所以不羅縷者，冀因結奏得從私願也。
units.en: Xie Jie suddenly blocked me; I had not argued every clause because I hoped his memorial would win me the ruling I sought.
units.literal: Yet Jie in one morning harshly thwarted your subject; the reason your subject earlier did not belabor detail was that I hoped through Jie's memorial my private wish might be granted.

units.zh: 今既所願不從，而敕雲但為過耳，非所不及也，以此見原。
units.en: Now my request is denied, yet the edict calls it a mere excess—not something beyond my duty—and forgives me on that ground.
units.literal: Now since what was wished is not followed, yet the edict says it was only excess, not what one could not reach, and by this pardons me.

units.zh: 臣忝司直之任，宜當正己率人，若其有過，不敢受原，是以申陳其愚。
units.en: I hold the post of censor-in-chief: I must set the example. If I was wrong I should not be excused, so I lay out my reasoning bluntly.
units.literal: Your subject disgraces the duty of director of correctness—ought to rectify self and lead others; if there is fault, I dare not accept pardon—therefore I declare this foolishness.

units.zh: 司隸與中丞俱共糾皇太子以下，則從皇太子以下無所不糾也。
units.en: If censor and colonel both impeach from the crown prince downward, nothing below that rank lies outside their reach.
units.literal: When colonel director of retainers and central censor together impeach from the crown prince down, then from the crown prince down there is nothing they do not impeach.

units.zh: 得糾皇太子而不得糾尚書，臣之暗塞既所未譬。
units.en: I may impeach the heir yet not the secretariat director—this blind spot I cannot understand.
units.literal: To be able to impeach the crown prince yet not be able to impeach the director of the secretariat—your subject's dim obstruction I have never grasped the parallel.

units.zh: 皇太子為在行馬之內邪，皇太子在行馬之內而得糾之，尚書在行馬之內而不得糾，無有此理。
units.en: Is the heir inside the corridor or not? If the heir inside may be impeached but the secretariat director inside may not, that rule does not exist.
units.literal: Is the crown prince inside the mounted corridor or not? If the crown prince inside the mounted corridor may be impeached, yet the director of the secretariat inside the mounted corridor may not be impeached—there is no such principle.

units.zh: 此理灼然，而結以此挫臣。
units.en: The logic is obvious, yet Xie Jie used it to block me.
units.literal: This principle is glaringly clear, yet Jie for this thwarted your subject.

units.zh: 臣可無恨耳，其於觀聽，無乃有怪邪！
units.en: I can swallow the insult—but will not the world find it absurd?
units.literal: Your subject may have no resentment—but for those who look and listen, is it not strange!

units.zh: 臣識石公前在殿上脫衣，為司隸荀愷所奏，先帝不以為非，于時莫謂侵官；
units.en: I recall when Lord Shi stripped in the hall and Xun Kai impeached him—the late emperor approved, and no one cried ‘overreach.’
units.literal: Your subject remembers when Lord Shi bared his torso in the hall, impeached by colonel director Xun Kai—the late emperor did not think it wrong; at the time none said it encroached on office;

units.zh: 今臣裁糾尚書，而當有罪乎？」
units.en: Am I now to be punished for impeaching only the secretariat director?"
units.literal: now when your subject only impeached the director of the secretariat, should there be guilt?"

units.zh: 咸累自上稱引故事，條理灼然，朝廷無以易之。
units.en: Fu Xian piled precedent on precedent until the case was airtight and the court could not refute him.
units.literal: Xian repeatedly cited himself to superior, adducing precedents; the ordering was clear and the court had no way to change it.

units.zh: 吳郡顧榮常與親故書曰：「傅長虞為司隸，勁直忠果，劾按驚人。
units.en: Gu Rong of Wu often wrote to friends and kin: "Fu Changyu as colonel director of retainers was forceful, upright, loyal, and resolute—his impeachments and investigations startled everyone.
units.literal: Gu Rong of Wu commandery often wrote to kinsmen and old friends, saying: "Fu Changyu as colonel director of retainers was forceful, straight, loyal, and resolute; his impeachments and investigations startled men.

units.zh: 雖非周才，偏亮可貴也。」
units.en: He was not a universal genius, but his moral brilliance was rare."
units.literal: Though not all-round talent, his partial brilliance is precious."

units.zh: 元康四年卒官，時年五十六，詔贈司隸校尉，朝服一具、衣一襲、錢二十萬，諡曰貞。
units.en: In the fourth year of the Yuankang era he died in office at fifty-six. An edict posthumously granted him colonel director of retainers, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and two hundred thousand cash, and gave him the posthumous name Zhen, "the steadfast."
units.literal: In the fourth year of the Yuankang era he died in office, aged fifty-six at the time; an edict posthumously granted him colonel director of retainers, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and two hundred thousand cash; his posthumous name was Zhen.

units.zh: 有三子：敷、晞、纂。
units.en: He left three sons: Fu, Xi, and Zuan.
units.literal: He had three sons: Fu, Xi, and Zuan.

units.zh: 長子敷嗣。
units.en: The eldest son, Fu, inherited his title.
units.literal: The eldest son Fu inherited.

units.zh: 敷字穎根，清靜有道，素解屬文。
units.en: Fu, courtesy name Yingen, was serene, reclusive, and a gifted writer.
units.literal: Fu's style name was Yingen; he was pure, quiet, and possessed the Way, by nature skilled at composing texts.

units.zh: 除太子舍人，轉尚書郎、太傅參軍，皆不起。
units.en: He was named attendant to the heir apparent, then secretary and staff officer to the grand tutor, but declined each post.
units.literal: He was appointed attendant to the heir apparent, transferred to gentleman of the secretariat and aide to the grand tutor, but on each occasion did not take up office.

units.zh: 永嘉之亂，避地會稽，元帝引為鎮東從事中郎。
units.en: When Yongjia brought chaos he fled to Kuaiji; Emperor Yuan summoned him as aide on the staff of the general who guards the east.
units.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil he fled to Kuaiji; Yuan-di summoned him as aide-de-camp on the staff of the general who garrisons the east.

units.zh: 素有贏疾，頻見敦喻，辭不獲免，輿病到職。
units.en: Chronic illness had long wasted him; though he begged off, he could not refuse and arrived in a sickbed litter to take office.
units.literal: By nature he had a wasting illness; repeatedly he was urged yet declined and could not escape; he took up duty sick in a litter.

units.zh: 數月卒，時年四十六。
units.en: Within months he was dead at forty-six.
units.literal: Before several months he died at age forty-six.

units.zh: 晞亦有才思，為上虞令，甚有政績，卒于司徒西曹屬。
units.en: Xi was also clever and thoughtful; as magistrate of Shangyu he earned praise for good rule, and died as an aide in the minister of education’s western bureau.
units.literal: Xi too had talent and thought; he was magistrate of Shangyu with very good administrative record, dying as an aide in the western bureau of the minister of education.

units.zh: 傅祗
units.en: Fu Zhi
units.literal: Fu Zhi.

units.zh: 祗字子莊。
units.en: Fu Zhi, courtesy name Zizhuang.
units.literal: Zhi's style name was Zizhuang.

units.zh: 父嘏，魏太常。
units.en: His father, Fu Gu, had been grand master of ceremonies under the Wei.
units.literal: His father was Gu, grand master of ceremonies of Wei.

units.zh: 祗性至孝，早知名，以才識明練稱。
units.en: Deeply filial and famous early, he was admired for shrewd, seasoned ability.
units.literal: Zhi by nature was utmost filial, early known by name, praised for talent, insight, clarity, and experience.

units.zh: 武帝始建東宮，起家太子舍人，累遷散騎黃門郎，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶。
units.en: When Emperor Wu of Jin founded the heir’s palace, Fu Zhi left mourning to become an heir’s attendant, rose to cavalier attendant and gentleman at the yellow gate, and received a secondary marquisate within the passes with three hundred households.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin first built the eastern palace, on leaving mourning he became attendant to the heir apparent; by stages he was promoted to cavalier attendant and gentleman at the yellow gate, enfeoffed secondary marquis within the passes with three hundred households' income.

units.zh: 母憂去職。
units.en: He resigned to mourn his mother.
units.literal: On his mother's bereavement he left office.

units.zh: 及葬母，詔給太常五等吉凶導從。
units.en: For her burial the court ordered the grand master of ceremonies to supply the full five-grade funeral escort.
units.literal: When burying his mother, an edict granted the grand master of ceremonies the five-grade auspicious and inauspicious escort squads.

units.zh: 其後諸卿夫人葬給導從，自此始也。
units.en: Later, when ministers’ wives were buried, they too received such escorts—the practice began with him.
units.literal: Afterwards when ministers' wives were buried they were given escort squads—this began here.

units.zh: 服終，為滎陽太守。
units.en: When mourning ended he became governor of Xingyang.
units.literal: When mourning ended he became governor of Xingyang.

units.zh: 自魏黃初大水之後，河濟泛溢，鄧艾嘗著《濟河論》，開石門而通之，至是復浸壞。
units.en: After Wei’s Huangchu flood the Yellow and Ji had burst their banks; Deng Ai’s treatise and the stone sluice he opened had long held the waters—by now the works had failed again.
units.literal: From after the great flood of Wei Huangchu, the Yellow and Ji rivers overflowed; Deng Ai once wrote the "On the Ji and Yellow Rivers," opening the stone gate to connect them—to this point they were again inundated and ruined.

units.zh: 祗乃造沈萊堰，至今兗、豫無水患，百姓為立碑頌焉。
units.en: Fu Zhi built the Shen and Lai embankments; Yan and Yu have been free of floods since, and the people raised a stele in his honor.
units.literal: Zhi thereupon built the Shen-Lai weirs; to this day Yan and Yu have no water harm; the hundred surnames erected a stele in praise.

units.zh: 尋表兼廷尉，遷常侍、左軍將軍。
units.en: Soon he added the post of commandant of justice, then became a regular attendant and general of the left army.
units.literal: Soon he memorialed to concurrently hold commandant of justice, was promoted to regular attendant and general of the left army.

units.zh: 及帝崩，梓宮在殯，而太傅楊駿輔政，欲悅眾心，議普進封爵。
units.en: While the emperor’s coffin still lay in mourning, Grand Tutor Yang Jun ran the government and proposed blanket promotions to buy popularity.
units.literal: When the emperor died, while the catalpa coffin was still in the mourning shed, grand tutor Yang Jun directed the government, wishing to please the multitude's hearts, debated universally advancing noble ranks.

units.zh: 祗與駿書曰：「未有帝王始崩，臣下論功者也。」
units.en: Fu Zhi wrote to Yang Jun: "No worthy court has ever handed out rewards for merit the moment an emperor dies."
units.literal: Zhi wrote to Jun: "Never yet has there been discussion of ministers' merits when an emperor has first died."

units.zh: 駿不從。
units.en: Jun ignored him.
units.literal: Jun did not follow.

units.zh: 入為侍中。
units.en: He was summoned to palace attendant.
units.literal: He entered as palace attendant.

units.zh: 時將誅駿，而駿不之知。
units.en: The coup against Jun was already set, yet Jun knew nothing.
units.literal: At the time they were about to execute Jun, yet Jun did not know it.

units.zh: 祗侍駿坐，而雲龍門閉，內外不通。
units.en: Fu Zhi was sitting with Jun when word came that the Dragon Gate was sealed and the palace cut off from the city.
units.literal: Zhi attended Jun seated, yet it was said the Dragon Gate was closed, inside and outside not communicating.

units.zh: 祗請與尚書武茂聽國家消息，揖而下階。
units.en: Fu Zhi asked to go with Wu Mao of the secretariat to learn the court’s fate, bowed, and stepped down from the hall.
units.literal: Zhi asked to go with Wu Mao of the secretariat to listen for news of the state, bowed and went down the steps.

units.zh: 茂猶坐，祗顧曰：「君非天子臣邪！
units.en: Wu Mao remained seated; Fu Zhi turned and cried, ‘Are you not a minister of the throne?’
units.literal: Mao still sat; Zhi looked back saying: "Are you not the Son of Heaven's minister!

units.zh: 今內外隔絕，不知國家所在，何得安坐！」
units.en: ‘Inside and outside are sealed—we do not even know where the sovereign is—how can you sit at ease?’"
units.literal: Now inside and outside are cut off; we do not know where the court is—how can you sit at ease!"

units.zh: 茂乃驚起。
units.en: Wu Mao leapt up in alarm.
units.literal: Mao then rose in alarm.

units.zh: 駿既伏誅，裴楷息瓚，駿之婿也，為亂兵所害。
units.en: When Jun fell, Pei Kai’s son Pei Zan—Jun’s son-in-law—was cut down by mutinous troops.
units.literal: After Jun was put to death, Pei Kai's son Zan, Jun's son-in-law, was killed by mutinous soldiers.

units.zh: 尚書左僕射荀愷與楷不平，因奏楷是駿親，收付廷尉。
units.en: Left vice-director Xun Kai, who hated Pei Kai, memorialized that Kai was Jun’s intimate and had him arrested for the commandant of justice.
units.literal: Vice-director of the secretariat, left, Xun Kai was not at peace with Kai, therefore memorialized that Kai was Jun's close kin and had him seized and handed to the commandant of justice.

units.zh: 祗證楷無罪，有詔赦之。
units.en: Fu Zhi testified that Pei Kai was innocent, and an edict freed him.
units.literal: Zhi testified that Kai had no crime; an edict pardoned him.

units.zh: 時又收駿官屬，祗復啟曰：「昔魯芝為曹爽司馬，斬關出赴爽，宣帝義之，尚遷青州刺史。
units.en: When Jun's staff were also arrested, Fu Zhi submitted another statement: "In the past Lu Zhi served as Sima to Cao Shuang, broke through the gates and rode out to join him, and Emperor Xuan approved his loyalty and still promoted him to inspector of Qingzhou.
units.literal: At the time they also seized Jun's subordinates; Zhi again stated: "In the past Lu Zhi was Sima to Cao Shuang, broke the gate bars and rode out to join Shuang—Emperor Xuan praised his righteousness and still promoted him to inspector of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 駿之僚佐不可加罰。」
units.en: Yang Jun’s aides should not be punished further."
units.literal: Jun's staff aides must not receive added punishment."

units.zh: 詔又赦之。
units.en: Another edict pardoned them.
units.literal: An edict again pardoned them.

units.zh: 祗多所維正皆如此。
units.en: Time and again Fu Zhi steadied justice in this way.
units.literal: Zhi's many upholdings of rectitude were all like this.

units.zh: 除河南尹，未拜，遷司隸校尉。
units.en: He was named governor of Henan but before taking office was made colonel director of retainers.
units.literal: He was appointed governor of Henan; before investiture he was promoted colonel director of retainers.

units.zh: 以討楊駿勳，當封郡公八千戶，固讓，減半，降封靈川縣公，千八百戶，餘二千二百戶封少子暢為武鄉亭侯。
units.en: For crushing Yang Jun he merited a commandery-duke’s fief of eight thousand households; he refused until the court halved it to a district duke of Lingchuan with eighteen hundred households and enfeoffed his youngest son Chang as village marquis of Wuxiang with the remainder.
units.literal: For merit in striking Yang Jun he ought to have been enfeoffed duke of a commandery with eight thousand households; he firmly declined, halved it, was demoted in enfeoffment to duke of Lingchuan district with one thousand eight hundred households, the remaining two thousand two hundred households enfeoffed his youngest son Chang as village marquis of Wuxiang.

units.zh: 又以本封賜兄子雋為東明亭侯。
units.en: From his original grant he also made his nephew Jun village marquis of Dongming.
units.literal: Further with his original fief he bestowed on elder brother's son Jun village marquis of Dongming.

units.zh: 楚王瑋之矯詔也，祗以聞奏稽留，免官。
units.en: When Prince Chu, Sima Wei, forged an edict, Fu Zhi was dismissed for slow reporting.
units.literal: When Prince Chu, Wei, forged the edict, Zhi because reporting was delayed was dismissed.

units.zh: 期年，遷光祿勳，復以公事免。
units.en: A year later he became grand master of splendid horses, then was removed again over a public affair.
units.literal: After a full year he was promoted grand master of splendid horses; again for public affairs he was dismissed.

units.zh: 氐人齊萬年舉兵反，以祗為行安西軍司，加常侍，率安西將軍夏侯駿討平之。
units.en: When the Di leader Qi Wannian rebelled, Fu Zhi served as acting chief of staff for the Army of the West with concurrent regular attendant, accompanying General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to crush the revolt.
units.literal: The Di man Qi Wannian raised troops in revolt; Zhi was made acting army director of Pacifying-the-West, with concurrent regular attendant, and led General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to strike and pacify him.

units.zh: 遷衛尉，以風疾遜位，就拜常侍，食卿祿秩，賜錢及床帳等。
units.en: Promoted commandant of the guards, he resigned with a palsy, was kept as regular attendant on ministerial salary, and given cash, bedding, and the like.
units.literal: He was promoted commandant of the guards, on wind illness yielded place, was then appointed regular attendant, ate ministerial salary ranks, was granted cash, bed-curtains, and so on.

units.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，門施行馬。
units.en: Soon he added the title grand counsellor of splendid horses and was allowed the mounted patrol barrier at his gate.
units.literal: Soon he was added grand counsellor of splendid horses; mounted patrol lanes were set up at his gate.

units.zh: 及趙王倫輔政，以為中書監，常侍如故，以鎮眾心。
units.en: When Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, took charge, he made Fu Zhi overseer of the secretariat, still a regular attendant, to calm public opinion.
units.literal: When Prince Zhao, Lun, directed the government, he made him overseer of the secretariat, regular attendant as before, to steady the host of hearts.

units.zh: 祗辭之以疾，倫遣御史輿祗就職。
units.en: Fu Zhi pleaded illness; Lun sent a censor with a litter to force him to his desk.
units.literal: Zhi declined on grounds of illness; Lun sent a censor to carry Zhi in a litter to take up office.

units.zh: 王戎、陳准等相與言曰：「傅公在事，吾屬無憂矣。」
units.en: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said to each other, ‘With Lord Fu at the helm we need not worry.’
units.literal: Wang Rong, Chen Zhun, and others spoke together: "With Lord Fu in charge, our sort has no worries."

units.zh: 其為物所倚信如此。
units.en: Such was the trust men placed in him.
units.literal: Thus he was trusted by others to this degree.

units.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。
units.en: When Lun seized the throne, Fu Zhi became right grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment and added palace attendant.
units.literal: When Lun usurped, he again was right grand master of splendid horses, established office, added palace attendant.

units.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。
units.en: After Emperor Hui returned, Fu Zhi asked to resign for having served the usurper; the court refused.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to the palace, Zhi because he had received illicit office asked to retire—not permitted.

units.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。
units.en: When Lun first usurped, Sun Xiu, Prince Yiyang Sima Wei, and a dozen others had drafted the abdication liturgy and text.
units.literal: At first when Lun usurped, Sun Xiu and Prince of Yiyang, Wei, and more than a dozen others pre-drafted the ceremonies and abdication texts.

units.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。
units.en: When Lun fell, Prince Qi Sima Jiong arrested Liu Dai, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others for the commandant of justice.
units.literal: When Lun fell, the prince of Qi, Jiong, seized palace attendant Liu Dai, regular attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, yellow gate gentleman Lu Ji, right aide Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.

units.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。
units.en: Because the abdication edict had issued from the secretariat, some wanted Fu Zhi punished, but a general amnesty spared him.
units.literal: Because the abdication text came from the secretariat, they again debated punishing Zhi's crime, but a general amnesty arrived and he was pardoned.

units.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。
units.en: Later it was shown the draft was not his hand, and an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.
units.literal: Later because the abdication draft in manuscript was not written by Zhi, thereupon an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.

units.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。
units.en: His son Fu Xuan married the princess of Hongnong.
units.literal: His son Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.

units.zh: 尋遷太子少傅，上章遜位還第。
units.en: Soon he became junior tutor to the heir apparent, then begged leave to retire home.
units.literal: Soon he was promoted junior tutor to the heir apparent; he submitted a memorial yielding office and returning home.

units.zh: 及成都王穎為太傅，復以祗為少傅，加侍中。
units.en: When Prince Chengdu Sima Ying became grand tutor, he again named Fu Zhi junior tutor with added palace attendant.
units.literal: When Prince Chengdu, Ying, was grand tutor, again he made Zhi junior tutor, added palace attendant.

units.zh: 懷帝即位，遷光祿大夫、侍中，未拜，加右僕射、中書監。
units.en: Under Emperor Huai he rose to grand counsellor of splendid horses and palace attendant, then—before the first appointment took effect—added right vice-director and overseer of the secretariat.
units.literal: When Emperor Huai mounted the throne, he was promoted grand counsellor of splendid horses and palace attendant; before investiture he was added right vice-director and overseer of the secretariat.

units.zh: 時太傅東海王越輔政，祗既居端右，每宣君臣謙光之道，由此上下雍穆。
units.en: While Grand Tutor Prince Donghai Sima Yue governed, Fu Zhi as senior minister on the right preached mutual deference between sovereign and ministers, and court relations grew calm.
units.literal: At that time grand tutor Prince of Donghai Yue directed the government; Zhi already stood at the head of the right—often he proclaimed the way of ruler and ministers yielding glory, and thereby above and below were harmonious and reverent.

units.zh: 祗明達國體，朝廷制度多所經綜。
units.en: He grasped how the state should run and had shaped many of its institutions.
units.literal: Zhi understood the state's body; many court systems he had managed and drawn together.

units.zh: 曆左光祿、開府，行太子太傅，侍中如故。
units.en: He passed through left grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment, acting grand tutor to the heir apparent, still a palace attendant.
units.literal: He served as left grand master of splendid horses, established office, acting grand tutor to the heir apparent, palace attendant as before.

units.zh: 疾篤遜位，不許。
units.en: Gravely ill, he asked to retire; the court refused.
units.literal: On grave illness he yielded office—not permitted.

units.zh: 遷司徒，以足疾，詔版輿上殿，不拜。
units.en: Raised to minister of education, he was carried in a litter to court because of his feet and excused from bowing.
units.literal: He was promoted minister of education; on foot ailment an edict ordered a litter to the hall; he did not bow.

units.zh: 大將軍苟晞表請遷都，使祗出詣河陰，修理舟楫，為水行之備。
units.en: General Gou Xi proposed moving the capital and sent Fu Zhi to Heyin to ready boats for a river retreat.
units.literal: Great general Gou Xi memorialized requesting removal of the capital, sent Zhi out to Heyin to repair boats and oars, preparing for travel by water.

units.zh: 及洛陽陷沒，遂共建行台，推祗為盟主，以司徒、持節、大都督諸軍事傳檄四方。
units.en: When Luoyang fell, the exiles set up a mobile command, chose Fu Zhi as their head, and issued calls in his name as minister of education, credential-bearing supreme commander.
units.literal: When Luoyang fell and was lost, they thereupon jointly set up a mobile headquarters, pushed Zhi to be covenant lord, transmitting proclamations in the four directions as minister of education, bearer of the staff of authority, grand governor of military affairs.

units.zh: 遣子宣將公主與尚書令和郁赴告方伯征義兵，祗自屯盟津小城，宣弟暢行河陰令，以待宣。
units.en: He sent Fu Xuan with the princess and He Yu, the director of the secretariat, to rally regional lords while he himself held the small fort at Meng Ford; his younger son Chang served as magistrate of Heyin to cover the crossing.
units.literal: He sent son Xuan leading the princess and Director of the secretariat He Yu to notify regional governors and summon righteous troops; Zhi himself camped at the small fort of Meng Ford; Xuan's younger brother Chang acted as magistrate of Heyin to await Xuan.

units.zh: 祗以暴疾薨，時年六十九。
units.en: Fu Zhi died of a sudden illness at sixty-nine.
units.literal: Zhi died of sudden illness at age sixty-nine.

units.zh: 祗自以義誠不終，力疾手筆敕厲其二子宣、暢，辭旨深切，覽者莫不感激慷慨。
units.en: Believing his duty of loyalty unfinished, he dragged himself from his sickbed to write a fierce testament for Xuan and Chang; every reader was moved to tears.
units.literal: Zhi himself thought his obligation of loyalty unfinished; with force of sickness he personally wrote in brush stern admonition to his two sons Xuan and Chang; the wording was bitter and deep, none who read it failed to be moved and roused.

units.zh: 祗著文章駁論十餘萬言。
units.en: He left more than a hundred thousand characters of essays and polemics.
units.literal: Zhi authored refutation essays of over a hundred thousand graphs.

units.zh: 宣字世弘。
units.en: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Shihong.
units.literal: Xuan's style name was Shihong.

units.zh: 年六歲喪繼母，哭泣如成人，中表異之。
units.en: At six he lost his stepmother and wept like a grown man; kinsfolk marveled.
units.literal: At age six he lost his stepmother; he wept like an adult, and cousins marveled.

units.zh: 及長，好學，趙王倫以為相國掾、尚書郎、太子中舍人，遷司徒西曹掾。
units.en: As an adult he loved books; Prince Zhao Lun made him aide to the minister of state, secretary, heir’s gentleman, then aide in the minister of education’s western bureau.
units.literal: When grown he loved learning; Prince Zhao Lun made him aide to the minister of state, gentleman of the secretariat, palace gentleman to the heir apparent; he was promoted aide in the western bureau of the minister of education.

units.zh: 去職，累遷為秘書丞、驃騎從事中郎。
units.en: After resigning he rose to secretary’s aide and staff officer to the general who gallops to battle.
units.literal: Leaving office, by stages he was promoted secretary assistant, aide-de-camp on the staff of the general who gallops to battle.

units.zh: 惠帝至自長安，以宣為左丞，不就，遷黃門郎。
units.en: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang’an, Fu Xuan was named left aide but declined, then was made gentleman at the yellow gate.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang-an, Xuan was made left aide—he did not take office—and was promoted gentleman at the yellow gate.

units.zh: 懷帝即位，轉吏部郎，又為御史中丞。
units.en: Under Emperor Huai he became a gentleman in the ministry of personnel, then metropolitan censor again.
units.literal: When Emperor Huai mounted the throne, he was transferred to gentleman of the ministry of personnel, again became metropolitan censor.

units.zh: 卒年四十九，無子，以暢子沖為嗣。
units.en: He died at forty-nine without a son, so his brother Chang’s son Chong inherited the line.
units.literal: He died at age forty-nine, without sons; Chang's son Chong was made heir.

units.zh: 暢字世道。
units.en: Fu Chang, courtesy name Shidao.
units.literal: Chang's style name was Shidao.

units.zh: 年五歲，父友見而戲之，解暢衣，取其金環與侍者，暢不之惜，以此賞之。
units.en: When he was five, a friend of his father teased him, stripped off his coat, and gave his gold ring to a servant; the boy showed no resentment, and adults praised his composure.
units.literal: At age five, a friend of his father saw him and teased him, stripped Chang's clothes, took his gold ring and gave it to a servant—Chang did not grudge it; for this they praised him.

units.zh: 年未弱冠，甚有重名。
units.en: Before he came of age he was already famous.
units.literal: Before the capping year he already had great reputation.

units.zh: 以選入侍講東宮，為秘書丞。
units.en: Chosen for the heir’s lecture staff, he became an assistant in the palace library.
units.literal: By selection he entered to lecture in the eastern palace, became secretary assistant.

units.zh: 尋沒于石勒，勒以為大將軍右司馬。
units.en: He soon fell into Shi Le’s hands; Le appointed him senior clerk on the right for the grand general.
units.literal: Soon he was lost to Shi Le; Le made him major on the right to the grand general.

units.zh: 諳識朝儀，恆居機密，勒甚重之。
units.en: Expert in court ritual and privy to every secret plan, he won Shi Le’s deep respect.
units.literal: Thoroughly versed in court ceremony, he always dwelt in secret matters; Le greatly esteemed him.

units.zh: 作《晉諸公敘贊》二十二卷，又為《公卿故事》九卷。
units.en: He wrote the Appraisal Narratives of Jin Lords in twenty-two scrolls and the Stories of Dukes and Ministers in nine.
units.literal: He composed Appraisal Narratives of Jin Lords in twenty-two fascicles, also Stories of Dukes and Ministers in nine fascicles.

units.zh: 咸和五年卒。
units.en: In the fifth year of Xianhe, he died.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xianhe, he died.

units.zh: 子詠，過江為交州刺史、太子右率。
units.en: His son Fu Yong crossed south to serve as inspector of Jiaozhou and commander of the heir’s right guard.
units.literal: His son Yong, crossing the river became inspector of Jiaozhou and leader of the right guard of the heir apparent.

units.zh: 【史評】
units.en: Section heading: editors’ appraisal.
units.literal: 【Historical appraisal】

units.zh: 史臣曰：武帝覽觀四方，平章百姓，永言啟沃，任切爭臣。
units.en: The historians write: Emperor Wu surveyed the realm and weighed the welfare of the people; longing for frank counsel, he charged his remonstrating ministers with a heavy trust.
units.literal: The history clerk says: Emperor Wu surveyed the four quarters and balanced assessment of the hundred surnames; ever speaking of opening and fertilizing, he entrusted a cutting task to ministers who contend.

units.zh: 傅玄體強直之姿，懷匪躬之操，抗辭正色，補闕弼違，諤諤當朝，不忝其職者矣。
units.en: Fu Xuan was rigid and upright, selfless in devotion, spoke his mind with stern dignity, and strove to mend faults at court—he did honor to his office.
units.literal: Fu Xuan embodied the posture of forceful straightness, cherished the integrity of not being for himself alone, resisted in words with upright countenance, mended omissions and aided against error; forthright in court, he did not disgrace his office.

units.zh: 及乎位居三獨，彈擊是司，遂能使台閣生風，貴戚斂手。
units.en: Once he held one of the three independent censorial posts and wielded the power of impeachment, the ministries stiffened with discipline and the great families pulled in their claws.
units.literal: When he reached office among the three independents and impeachment was his charge, then he could make the bureaus catch a new wind and noble in-laws draw in their hands.

units.zh: 雖前代鮑、葛，何以加之！
units.en: Even Han’s Bao Xuan and Ge Ying would not have surpassed him.
units.literal: Even the Bao and Ge of former dynasties—how could one add beyond them!

units.zh: 然而惟此褊心，乏弘雅之度，驟聞競爽，為物議所譏，惜哉！
units.en: Yet his narrow temper lacked easy magnanimity; quick to bristle at rivals, he earned public ridicule—a pity.
units.literal: Yet only this narrow mind lacked breadth in magnanimous demeanor; abruptly hearing rival brilliance, he was mocked by public opinion—pity!

units.zh: 古人取戒于韋弦，良有以也。
units.en: The ancients took both the soft leather and the tight bowstring as their teachers—how true that remains.
units.literal: The ancients took warning from leather and bowstring—truly there was reason.

units.zh: 長虞風格凝峻，弗墜家聲。
units.en: Fu Xian’s manner was grave and austere; he did not shame his father’s name.
units.literal: Changyu's manner was concentrated and stern; he did not let the family reputation fall.

units.zh: 及其納諫汝南，獻書臨晉，居諒直之地，有先見之明矣。
units.en: When he pressed his advice on the king of Runan and sent his memorials from the Linjin command, he stood in the place of blunt loyalty and showed real foresight.
units.literal: When it came to his offering remonstrance at Runan and presenting writings at Linjin, occupying a place of honesty and straightness, he had foresight indeed.

units.zh: 傅祗名父之子，早樹風猷，崎嶇危亂之朝，匡救君臣之際，卒能保全祿位，可謂有道存焉。
units.en: Fu Zhi, son of a famous minister, showed his quality early; through a time of coups and chaos he steadied sovereign and subject and kept his honor and salary—clearly the Way lived in him.
units.literal: Fu Zhi, son of a renowned father, early set his course; in a court rugged with peril he righted ruler and minister at the crisis, and in the end could preserve rank and stipend—one may say the Way was in him.

units.zh: 贊曰：鶉觚貞諒，實惟朝望。
units.en: The encomium reads: The baron of Chungu, steadfast and true, was indeed the court’s moral backbone.
units.literal: Encomium says: Chungu's steadfast loyalty—truly a pillar of the court.

units.zh: 志厲強直，性乖夷曠。
units.en: His will was fierce and upright; his temper turned away from easy-going tolerance.
units.literal: His will was stern with straightness; his nature ran against easy breadth.

units.zh: 長虞剛簡，無虧風尚。
units.en: Fu Xian’s stern simplicity never betrayed the family’s standards.
units.literal: Changyu was stern and simple, without loss to conduct.

units.zh: 子莊才識，爰膺袞職。
units.en: Fu Zhi, styled Zizhuang, matched talent to insight and shouldered the highest offices.
units.literal: Zizhuang's talent and insight—then bore the robes of office.

units.zh: 忠績未申，泉途遽逼。=
units.en: His loyal service was cut short; the road to the grave came all too soon.
units.literal: Loyal deeds not fully declared, the road to the springs pressed suddenly.
